1.8.m: Therefore, in the circumstances mentioned, they must be guarded by restraint and blows; / and blows should be applied appropriately in season and as is fitting.

1.8.s:
parigṛhya bahūndārānupacāraiḥ samo bhavet .
yathākramocitaiḥ karma dānasatkāravāsanaiḥ . . 27
1.8.d:
परिगृह्य बहून्दारानुपचारैः समो भवेत् ।
यथाक्रमोचितैः कर्म दानसत्कारवासनैः ॥ 27
1.8.m: Having taken multiple wives, one should be impartial in conduct toward them, / in work, gifts, respect, and residences appropriate according to proper order.

1.8.s:
prathamo'bhijano dharmo yogyatvaṃ ca suputratā .
pakṣe vittaṃ viśetstrīṇāṃ mānastatkāraṇaṃ tathā . . 28
1.8.d:
प्रथमोऽभिजनो धर्मो योग्यत्वं च सुपुत्रता ।
पक्षे वित्तं विशेत्स्त्रीणां मानस्तत्कारणं तथा ॥ 28
1.8.m: Lineage is foremost, then righteousness, fitness, and having good sons; / wealth belongs to a woman's side, and respect is grounded therein.

1.8.s:
tasmānmāno na kartavyo heyaścāpi na tatkṛtaḥ .
gurutve lāghave vāpi satāṃ kāryaṃ nibandhanam . . 29
1.8.d:
तस्मान्मानो न कर्तव्यो हेयश्चापि न तत्कृतः ।
गुरुत्वे लाघवे वापि सतां कार्यं निबन्धनम् ॥ 29
1.8.m: Therefore, unjustified respect should not be shown, nor should what is due be withheld; / in showing weight or slight, good men must have a substantial ground.

1.8.s:
ākasmike prayuñjānaḥ prekṣāvānmānalāghave .
sa yatkiñcanakāritvāccāyamevaiti lāghavam . . 1.8.30
1.8.d:
आकस्मिके प्रयुञ्जानः प्रेक्षावान्मानलाघवे ।
स यत्किञ्चनकारित्वाच्चायमेवैति लाघवम् ॥ 1.8.30
1.8.m: A discerning man who dispenses honor or slight on a sudden whim, / because he acts recklessly, comes to be slighted himself.

1.8.s:
yathā mānāpamānau hi prayujyetānimittataḥ .
tannimittā janatyāge prayatante tadāśritāḥ . . 31
1.8.d:
यथा मानापमानौ हि प्रयुज्येतानिमित्ततः ।
तन्निमित्ता जनत्यागे प्रयतन्ते तदाश्रिताः ॥ 31
1.8.m: For when honour and dishonour are bestowed without reason, / his dependants strive to abandon him because of it.

1.8.s:
etadeva hyapatyānāṃ1 jñeyaṃ mānanakāraṇam .
yatsvāpatyanimitteṣu2 pradhāne kulayogyate . . 32
1.8.d:
एतदेव ह्यपत्यानां1 ज्ञेयं माननकारणम् ।
यत्स्वापत्यनिमित्तेषु2 प्रधाने कुलयोग्यते ॥ 32
1.8.m: This very ground is to be known as the cause for respecting children: / that fitness of family is paramount in matters concerning one's own offspring.

1.8.s:
tatsaṃyogātsukhaṃ puṃsāṃ mahadduḥkhaṃ viyogataḥ .
tatprāptiḥ prati hātavyā svārthāyaiva priyāṇyapi . . 33
1.8.d:
तत्संयोगात्सुखं पुंसां महद्दुःखं वियोगतः ।
तत्प्राप्तिः प्रति हातव्या स्वार्थायैव प्रियाण्यपि ॥ 33
1.8.m: From union with them comes happiness to men; great sorrow from separation; / in order to attain them, even dear things are to be relinquished for one's own sake.

1.8.s:
ataḥ svārthaikaniṣṭho'yaṃ lokaḥ sarvo'vasīyate .
tatprasiddhirbhavedastamānād bhrāntividhāyakaḥ . . 34
1.8.d:
अतः स्वार्थैकनिष्ठोऽयं लोकः सर्वोऽवसीयते ।
तत्प्रसिद्धिर्भवेदस्तमानाद् भ्रान्तिविधायकः ॥ 34
1.8.m: Hence this entire world is seen to be dedicated solely to self-interest; / when its attainment fades, it gives rise to delusion.

1.8.s:
tato dārādikā bhṛtyā niyantavyāstathā dvijāḥ .
yathehāmutra vā śreyaḥ prāpnuyāduttarottaram . . 35
1.8.d:
ततो दारादिका भृत्या नियन्तव्यास्तथा द्विजाः ।
यथेहामुत्र वा श्रेयः प्राप्नुयादुत्तरोत्तरम् ॥ 35
1.8.m: Therefore, wives and other dependents, as well as twice-born folk, should be restrained, / so that one may attain increasing welfare here and in the hereafter.

1.8.s:
strīṇāṃ dharmārthakāmeṣu nātisandhānamācaret .
tāsāṃ teṣvabhisandhānādbhavedātmābhisaṃhitaḥ . . 36
1.8.d:
स्त्रीणां धर्मार्थकामेषु नातिसन्धानमाचरेत् ।
तासां तेष्वभिसन्धानाद्भवेदात्माभिसंहितः ॥ 36
1.8.m: One should not practice deceit against women in dharma, wealth, and desire; / from deceit toward them in these matters, oneself becomes ruined.

1.8.s:
jāyā tvardhaṃ śarīrasya nṛṇāṃ dharmādisādhane .
nātastāsu vyathāṃ kāñcitpratikūlaṃ samācaret . . 37
1.8.d:
जाया त्वर्धं शरीरस्य नृणां धर्मादिसाधने ।
नातस्तासु व्यथां काञ्चित्प्रतिकूलं समाचरेत् ॥ 37
1.8.m: For a wife is half the body of men in accomplishing dharma and the rest; / hence, one should never inflict any distress or hostility upon them.

1.8.s:
yajñotsavādau nākasmātkāñcidāsāṃ viśeṣayet .
vastratāmbūladānādau pratipattau samo bhavet . . 38
1.8.d:
यज्ञोत्सवादौ नाकस्मात्काञ्चिदासां विशेषयेत् ।
वस्त्रताम्बूलदानादौ प्रतिपत्तौ समो भवेत् ॥ 38
1.8.m: In sacrifices, festivals, and the like, he should not arbitrarily favour any one of them; / in gifts of garments, betel, and the like, and in respectful treatment, he should be impartial.

1.8.s:
priyāpriyatvaṃ bhedo hi kāmatastu rahogataḥ .
upacāraiḥ punarvākyaistulyavṛttiḥ praśasyate . . 39
1.8.d:
प्रियाप्रियत्वं भेदो हि कामतस्तु रहोगतः ।
उपचारैः पुनर्वाक्यैस्तुल्यवृत्तिः प्रशस्यते ॥ 39
1.8.m: Partiality or dislike, indeed, belongs to desire when in private; / in social conduct and words, however, equal behaviour is praised.

1.8.s:
ārtave tu punaḥ sarvā upagamyāḥ priyā iva .
pūrvābhijātadharmārthā putriṇī cottarottaram . . 1.8.40
1.8.d:
आर्तवे तु पुनः सर्वा उपगम्याः प्रिया इव ।
पूर्वाभिजातधर्मार्था पुत्रिणी चोत्तरोत्तरम् ॥ 1.8.40
1.8.m: In their fertile seasons, all should be approached as beloved, / in proper succession: the first married, of noble birth, for dharma and wealth, and the mother of sons.

1.8.s:
udaggacchedanenaiva vidhinā nityamārtave .
tulyavṛttiryathākālaṃ svaṃ svaṃ vāsamakhaṇḍayan . . 41
1.8.d:
उदग्गच्छेदनेनैव विधिना नित्यमार्तवे ।
तुल्यवृत्तिर्यथाकालं स्वं स्वं वासमखण्डयन् ॥ 41
1.8.m: He should proceed according to this very rule always during their fertile seasons, / maintaining equal conduct in due season, not omitting his visit to each.

1.8.s:
nityaparyāyavāsānāmapādānamasūnviduḥ .
ṛtuduḥkhaṃ pramodaśca tathā pūrvaṃ samāgataḥ . . 42
1.8.d:
नित्यपर्यायवासानामपादानमसून्विदुः ।
ऋतुदुःखं प्रमोदश्च तथा पूर्वं समागतः ॥ 42
1.8.m: They consider the deprivation of regular rotation of visits to be like death; / there is pain during the fertile season, and delight when he has arrived before.

1.8.s:
anyayā saha yadduḥkhaṃ sadasadvā rahogatam .
utkaṇṭhitaṃ vā yatkiñcitsapatnīṣu na tadvaset . . 43
1.8.d:
अन्यया सह यद्दुःखं सदसद्वा रहोगतम् ।
उत्कण्ठितं वा यत्किञ्चित्सपत्नीषु न तद्वसेत् ॥ 43
1.8.m: Whatever distress, good or bad, occurred in secret with another [wife], / or whatever longing arose, he should not reveal it among co-wives.

1.8.s:
yatkiñcidanyasambaddhamanyathā kathitaṃ mithaḥ .
tasya kuryādanirvedamātmanaiva vicintayet . . 44
1.8.d:
यत्किञ्चिदन्यसम्बद्धमन्यथा कथितं मिथः ।
तस्य कुर्यादनिर्वेदमात्मनैव विचिन्तयेत् ॥ 44
1.8.m: Whatever was spoken in confidence concerning another in a distorted way, / he should not give way to despair over it, but reflect upon it by himself.

1.8.s:
anyo'nyamatsarākhyānairna tā vācāpi bhartsayet .
guṇadoṣau ca vijñāya svayaṃ kuryānna niṣkalau . . 45
1.8.d:
अन्योऽन्यमत्सराख्यानैर्न ता वाचापि भर्त्सयेत् ।
गुणदोषौ च विज्ञाय स्वयं कुर्यान्न निष्कलौ ॥ 45
1.8.m: He should not rebuke them even in words over tales of mutual envy; / knowing their merits and faults, he should not make them fruitless.

1.8.s:
vastrālaṅkārabhojyādau tadapatyeṣvanukramāt .
mātṛdoṣānanādṛtya tulyadṛṣṭiḥ pitā bhavet . . 46
1.8.d:
वस्त्रालङ्कारभोज्यादौ तदपत्येष्वनुक्रमात् ।
मातृदोषाननादृत्य तुल्यदृष्टिः पिता भवेत् ॥ 46
1.8.m: In clothing, ornaments, food, and the like, regarding their offspring in proper order, / disregarding the mothers' faults, a father should be impartial.

1.8.s:
anyasyānyagatairdoṣairdūṣaṇaṃ na hi nītimat .
yattu teṣāmapatyaṃ tu tattulyamubhayorapi . . 47
1.8.d:
अन्यस्यान्यगतैर्दोषैर्दूषणं न हि नीतिमत् ।
यत्तु तेषामपत्यं तु तत्तुल्यमुभयोरपि ॥ 47
1.8.m: For reproaching someone with the faults of another is not prudent; / while the child born to them belongs equally to both.

1.8.s:
prītiṃ dveṣamabhiprāyaṃ śaucāśaucagatāgamān .
bahirantaśca jānīyāddāsa gūḍhacaraiḥ sadā . . 48
1.8.d:
प्रीतिं द्वेषमभिप्रायं शौचाशौचगतागमान् ।
बहिरन्तश्च जानीयाद्दास गूढचरैः सदा ॥ 48
1.8.m: Affection, hatred, intentions, purity and impurity, movements outside and inside, / he should constantly ascertain by means of male and female servants as secret agents.

1.8.s:
ātmānamapi vijñāya cittavṛtteranīśvaram .
viśvaseta kathaṃ strīṣu sarvāvinayadhāmasu . . 49
1.8.d:
आत्मानमपि विज्ञाय चित्तवृत्तेरनीश्वरम् ।
विश्वसेत कथं स्त्रीषु सर्वाविनयधामसु ॥ 49
1.8.m: Knowing that even oneself is not master of the movements of one's own mind, / how could one trust women, who are the abode of all indiscipline?

1.8.s:
vṛddhadāsyaḥ kramāyātā dhātryaśca paricārikāḥ .
tanmātṛpitṛkādyāśca ṣaṇḍavṛddhāścarā matāḥ . . 1.8.50
1.8.d:
वृद्धदास्यः क्रमायाता धात्र्यश्च परिचारिकाः ।
तन्मातृपितृकाद्याश्च षण्डवृद्धाश्चरा मताः ॥ 1.8.50
1.8.m: Old female slaves, hereditary wet-nurses, handmaids, / parents of these servants, and elderly eunuchs are considered spies.

1.8.s:
vividhaistatkathākhyānaistulyaśīladayānvitaiḥ .
praviśyāntarabhiprāyaṃ vidyātkāle prayojitaiḥ . . 51
1.8.d:
विविधैस्तत्कथाख्यानैस्तुल्यशीलदयान्वितैः ।
प्रविश्यान्तरभिप्रायं विद्यात्काले प्रयोजितैः ॥ 51
1.8.m: Through diverse narrations and tales, endowed with similar temperament and kindness, / entering into their inner intention, employed at the proper time, they should discover it.

1.8.s:
teṣu teṣu kathārtheṣu kathyamāneṣu lakṣayet .
mukhākārādibhirliṅgairabhiprāyaṃ manogatam . . 52
1.8.d:
तेषु तेषु कथार्थेषु कथ्यमानेषु लक्षयेत् ।
मुखाकारादिभिर्लिङ्गैरभिप्रायं मनोगतम् ॥ 52
1.8.m: While those various topics of conversation are being spoken, he should observe / the intention situated in the heart through bodily signs such as facial expressions.

1.8.s:
sītārundhatisambandhaistathā śākuntalādibhiḥ .
sadasaccaritākhyānairbhāvaṃ vidyātpravṛttitaḥ . . 53
1.8.d:
सीतारुन्धतिसम्बन्धैस्तथा शाकुन्तलादिभिः ।
सदसच्चरिताख्यानैर्भावं विद्यात्प्रवृत्तितः ॥ 53
1.8.m: Through stories connected with Sītā and Arundhatī, as well as Śakuntalā and others, / and through tales of good and bad conduct, he should discern her inner disposition from her reactions.

1.8.s:
tadduṣṭānāmaduṣṭeṣu sādhūnāmitareṣu ca .
prītiḥ kathāprabandheṣu syātsakhyaṃ puruṣeṣvitaḥ . . 54
1.8.d:
तद्दुष्टानामदुष्टेषु साधूनामितरेषु च ।
प्रीतिः कथाप्रबन्धेषु स्यात्सख्यं पुरुषेष्वितः ॥ 54
1.8.m: Corrupt women take delight in corrupt tales, and virtuous women in other kinds; / from this, affection may be known, and friendship among men.

1.8.s:
evamāgamaduṣṭābhyāmanumityā ca tattvataḥ .
strīṇāṃ viditvābhiprāyaṃ vartetāśu yathocitam . . 55
1.8.d:
एवमागमदुष्टाभ्यामनुमित्या च तत्त्वतः ।
स्त्रीणां विदित्वाभिप्रायं वर्तेताशु यथोचितम् ॥ 55
1.8.m: Having thus accurately understood the intention of women through scripture, observation of faults, and inference, / he should act promptly as is fitting.

1.8.s:
strībhyo vipratipannābhyaḥ prāṇairapi viyojanam .
dṛṣṭaṃ hi ca yathā 1 rājñāmato rakṣetprayatnataḥ . . 56
1.8.d:
स्त्रीभ्यो विप्रतिपन्नाभ्यः प्राणैरपि वियोजनम् ।
दृष्टं हि च यथा 1 राज्ञामतो रक्षेत्प्रयत्नतः ॥ 56
1.8.m: For it is seen that even loss of life comes to kings from estranged women; / therefore, one should guard [oneself] with diligence.

1.8.s:
veṇyā gūḍhena śastreṇa hato rājā śubhadhvajaḥ .
mekhalāmaṇinā devyā sauvīraśca narādhipaḥ . . 57
1.8.d:
वेण्या गूढेन शस्त्रेण हतो राजा शुभध्वजः ।
मेखलामणिना देव्या सौवीरश्च नराधिपः ॥ 57
1.8.m: King Śubhadhvaja was slain by a weapon concealed in a braid of hair; / and the king of the Sauvīras was killed by the queen with a jewel from her girdle.

1.8.s:
bhrātrā devīprayuktena bhadraseno nipātitaḥ .
tathā putreṇa kārūṣo ghātito darpaṇāsinā . . 58
1.8.d:
भ्रात्रा देवीप्रयुक्तेन भद्रसेनो निपातितः ।
तथा पुत्रेण कारूषो घातितो दर्पणासिना ॥ 58
1.8.m: Bhadrasena was struck down by his brother employed by the queen; / likewise, the king of Karūṣa was slain by his son with a sword [hidden in] a mirror.

1.8.s:
dvau kāśirājau vai vandyau cānandāpurayoṣitā .
viṣaṃ prayujya pañcatvamānītau pūjitātmakau . . 59
1.8.d:
द्वौ काशिराजौ वै वन्द्यौ चानन्दापुरयोषिता ।
विषं प्रयुज्य पञ्चत्वमानीतौ पूजितात्मकौ ॥ 59
1.8.m: Two venerable kings of Kāśi, venerable in their nature, / were brought to death by a woman of Ānandapura administering poison.

1.8.s:
evamādi mahābhāgā rājāno brāhmaṇāśca ha .
strībhiryatra nipātyante tatrānyeṣviha kā kathā . . 1.8.60
1.8.d:
एवमादि महाभागा राजानो ब्राह्मणाश्च ह ।
स्त्रीभिर्यत्र निपात्यन्ते तत्रान्येष्विह का कथा ॥ 1.8.60
1.8.m: When even such illustrious kings and brāhmaṇas / are brought down by women, what need be said of others here?

1.8.s:
tasmānnityāpramattena jāyā rakṣyāśca nityaśaḥ .
yathāvadupacaryāśca guṇadoṣānurūpataḥ . . 61
1.8.d:
तस्मान्नित्याप्रमत्तेन जाया रक्ष्याश्च नित्यशः ।
यथावदुपचर्याश्च गुणदोषानुरूपतः ॥ 61
1.8.m: Therefore, being ever vigilant, one must always protect one's wife / and attend to her properly according to her merits and faults.

1.8.s:
vaiṣamyādupacārāṇāṃ vikāraiścānimittajaiḥ .
viśeṣeṇa sapatnīkairakasmāccāpi vedanaiḥ . . 62
1.8.d:
वैषम्यादुपचाराणां विकारैश्चानिमित्तजैः ।
विशेषेण सपत्नीकैरकस्माच्चापि वेदनैः ॥ 62
1.8.m: Through disparity in treatment, through changes [of mood] arising without cause, / especially through co-wives, and through sudden afflictions,

1.8.s:
asambhāge ca vāgdaṇḍapāruṣyādaprasaṅgataḥ .
pradveṣo bhartari strīṇāṃ prakopaścāpi jāyate . . 63
1.8.d:
असम्भागे च वाग्दण्डपारुष्यादप्रसङ्गतः ।
प्रद्वेषो भर्तरि स्त्रीणां प्रकोपश्चापि जायते ॥ 63
1.8.m: and through lack of [sexual] union, harshness of words and punishment, and lack of affection, / hatred and great anger toward the husband arise in women.

1.8.s:
tataścāyāti vārdhakyamudvoḍhuścāpi śatrutām .
tasmānna tānprayuñjīta doṣāndāravināśakān . . 64
1.8.d:
ततश्चायाति वार्धक्यमुद्वोढुश्चापि शत्रुताम् ।
तस्मान्न तान्प्रयुञ्जीत दोषान्दारविनाशकान् ॥ 64
1.8.m: From that, old age comes [prematurely], and enmity toward the husband; / therefore, one should not employ those faults that destroy one's wife.

1.8.s:
na caitāḥ svakulācāramadharmaṃ vāpi cāñjasā .
na guṇāṃścāpyupekṣante prakṛtyā kimu pīḍitāḥ . . 65
1.8.d:
न चैताः स्वकुलाचारमधर्मं वापि चाञ्जसा ।
न गुणांश्चाप्युपेक्षन्ते प्रकृत्या किमु पीडिताः ॥ 65
1.8.m: By nature, these women do not readily disregard their family custom, nor unrighteousness, / nor virtues; how much less when they are oppressed?

1.8.s:
satītve prāyaśaḥ strīṇāṃ pradṛṣṭaṃ kāraṇatrayam .
parapuṃsāmasamprītiḥ priye prītiḥ svarakṣaṇe . . 66
1.8.d:
सतीत्वे प्रायशः स्त्रीणां प्रदृष्टं कारणत्रयम् ।
परपुंसामसम्प्रीतिः प्रिये प्रीतिः स्वरक्षणे ॥ 66
1.8.m: Three causes are generally seen for chastity in women: / lack of affection for other men, love for the beloved [husband], and self-protection.

1.8.s:
tasmātsurakṣitā nityamupacārairyathocitaiḥ .
subhṛtā1 nityakarmāṇaḥ kartavyā yoṣitaḥ sadā . . 67
1.8.d:
तस्मात्सुरक्षिता नित्यमुपचारैर्यथोचितैः ।
सुभृता1 नित्यकर्माणः कर्तव्या योषितः सदा ॥ 67
1.8.m: Therefore, well-guarded always with proper attentions / and well-maintained, women must ever be made to perform their daily duties.

1.8.s:
uttamāṃ sāmadānābhyāṃ madhyamābhyāṃ tu madhyamām .
paścimābhyāmubhāmyāṃ ca adhamāṃ samprasādhayet . . 68
1.8.d:
उत्तमां सामदानाभ्यां मध्यमाभ्यां तु मध्यमाम् ।
पश्चिमाभ्यामुभाम्यां च अधमां सम्प्रसाधयेत् ॥ 68
1.8.m: One should win over an excellent woman by conciliation and gifts; an intermediate one by the middle two [means]; / and a base one by both of the last two [means].

1.8.s:
bhedadaṇḍau prayujyāpi prāgapatyādyapekṣayā .
tacchiṣṭānāṃ tadā paścātsāmadānaprasādhane . . 69
1.8.d:
भेददण्डौ प्रयुज्यापि प्रागपत्याद्यपेक्षया ।
तच्छिष्टानां तदा पश्चात्सामदानप्रसाधने ॥ 69
1.8.m: Even after applying division and punishment out of prior consideration for children and the like, / the winning over of those remaining is then accomplished through conciliation and gifts.

1.8.s:
yāstu vidhvastacāritrā bhartuścāhitakārikāḥ .
tyājyā evaṃ striyaḥ sadbhiḥ2 kālakūṭaviṣopamāḥ . . 70
1.8.d:
यास्तु विध्वस्तचारित्रा भर्तुश्चाहितकारिकाः ।
त्याज्या एवं स्त्रियः सद्भिः2 कालकूटविषोपमाः ॥ 70
1.8.m: Those women whose conduct is ruined and who work injury to their husbands, / being like the kālakūṭa poison, must be abandoned by the good.

1.8.s:
iṣṭāḥ 3 kulodgatāḥ sādhvyo vinītā bhartṛvatsalāḥ .
sarvadā sādhanīyāstāḥ sampradāyottarottaraiḥ 4. . 71
1.8.d:
इष्टाः 3 कुलोद्गताः साध्व्यो विनीता भर्तृवत्सलाः ।
सर्वदा साधनीयास्ताः सम्प्रदायोत्तरोत्तरैः 4॥ 71
1.8.m: Beloved, born of good families, virtuous, modest, and devoted to their husbands— / such women should always be won over by ever higher traditions [of conduct].

1.8.s:
evameva yathoddiṣṭaṃ strīvṛttaṃ yo'nutiṣṭhati .
prāpnotyeva sa sampūrṇaṃ trivargaṃ 5 lokasambhavam . . 72
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi vivāhadharmeṣu
strīviṣaye naravṛttavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭamo'dhyāyaḥ . 8 .
āgamapraśaṃsāvarṇanam
1.8.d:
एवमेव यथोद्दिष्टं स्त्रीवृत्तं योऽनुतिष्ठति ।
प्राप्नोत्येव स सम्पूर्णं त्रिवर्गं 5 लोकसम्भवम् ॥ 72
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि विवाहधर्मेषु
स्त्रीविषये नरवृत्तवर्णनं नामाष्टमोऽध्यायः । 8 ।
आगमप्रशंसावर्णनम्
1.8.m:
He who thus observes the conduct regarding women as taught / attains the complete threefold aim [of life] that arises in the world.
Thus ends the eighth chapter, named “Description of Man’s Conduct Toward Women” in the rules of marriage in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-thousand [verses].
Description of the Praise of Scripture

1.9.s:
brahmovāca
evaṃ strīṣu manuṣyāṇāṃ vṛttiruktā samāsataḥ .
sāmprataṃ ca manuṣyeṣu strīṇāṃ samupadiśyate . . 1
1.9.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
एवं स्त्रीषु मनुष्याणां वृत्तिरुक्ता समासतः ।
साम्प्रतं च मनुष्येषु स्त्रीणां समुपदिश्यते ॥ 1
1.9.m:
Brahmā said:
Thus has the conduct of men toward women been declared in brief; / and now the conduct of women toward men is taught.

1.9.s:
samyagārādhanātpuṃsāṃ ratirvṛttiśca yoṣitaḥ .
putrāḥ svargādyadṛṣṭaṃ ca tasmādiṣṭo hi tadvidhiḥ . . 2
1.9.d:
सम्यगाराधनात्पुंसां रतिर्वृत्तिश्च योषितः ।
पुत्राः स्वर्गाद्यदृष्टं च तस्मादिष्टो हि तद्विधिः ॥ 2
1.9.m: From proper worship of men come sexual pleasure and maintenance for a woman, / sons, heaven, and the unseen [spiritual fruit]; therefore, the rule concerning that is desired.

1.9.s:
kartavyaṃ nāma yatkiñcitsarvaṃ 1 vidhimapekṣate .
vyaktimāyāti vaiphalyaṃ tadevārabdhamanyathā . . 3
1.9.d:
कर्तव्यं नाम यत्किञ्चित्सर्वं 1 विधिमपेक्षते ।
व्यक्तिमायाति वैफल्यं तदेवारब्धमन्यथा ॥ 3
1.9.m: Whatever duty is to be done depends entirely upon rule; / that very [undertaking], if begun otherwise, comes visibly to futility.

1.9.s:
vidhyapekṣīṇi sarvāṇi kāryāṇyaviphalānyapi .
hetubhūtāstrivargasya mahārambhā viśeṣataḥ . .4
1.9.d:
विध्यपेक्षीणि सर्वाणि कार्याण्यविफलान्यपि ।
हेतुभूतास्त्रिवर्गस्य महारम्भा विशेषतः ॥4
1.9.m: All actions, even those not fruitless, depend upon rules, / especially great undertakings that are the causes of the threefold aim [of life].

1.9.s:
sarvasādhyāvidhijñānamāgamaikanibandhanam .
sādhyaṃ dṛṣṭamadṛṣṭaṃ ca dvayaṃ vidhiniṣedhayoḥ . . 5
1.9.d:
सर्वसाध्याविधिज्ञानमागमैकनिबन्धनम् ।
साध्यं दृष्टमदृष्टं च द्वयं विधिनिषेधयोः ॥ 5
1.9.m: Knowledge of the rules for all that is to be accomplished depends solely upon scripture; / the two—both the seen and unseen [fruit] of injunction and prohibition—are what is to be accomplished.

1.9.s:
śāstrādhikāro na strīṇāṃ na granthānāṃ ca dhāraṇe .
tasmādihānye manyante tacchāsanamanarthakam . . 6
1.9.d:
शास्त्राधिकारो न स्त्रीणां न ग्रन्थानां च धारणे ।
तस्मादिहान्ये मन्यन्ते तच्छासनमनर्थकम् ॥ 6
1.9.m: Women have no qualification for the sacred texts, nor for retaining the treatises; / therefore, others here think that instruction for them is purposeless.

1.9.s:
āgamaikakriyāyoge strīṇāmadhyadhikāritā .
mṛte bhartari sādhvī syādityādau smṛtibhāṣitam . . 7
1.9.d:
आगमैकक्रियायोगे स्त्रीणामध्यधिकारिता ।
मृते भर्तरि साध्वी स्यादित्यादौ स्मृतिभाषितम् ॥ 7
1.9.m: In the performance of rites based solely on scripture, women also have qualification; / as stated in the smṛti: “When the husband dies, she should be virtuous,” and so on.

1.9.s:
tasmātkāryamakāryaṃ vā vijñāya prabhurāgamāt .
guṇadoṣeṣu tāḥ samyakchāsti rājā prajā iva . . 8
1.9.d:
तस्मात्कार्यमकार्यं वा विज्ञाय प्रभुरागमात् ।
गुणदोषेषु ताः सम्यक्छास्ति राजा प्रजा इव ॥ 8
1.9.m: Therefore, knowing from scripture what is to be done or not to be done, the master / governs them properly in their virtues and faults, just as a king governs his subjects.

1.9.s:
satyeva pramadāḥ kāścidviśeṣādhigatāgamāḥ .
yattu śāstrādhikāritvaṃ vacanaṃ syānnirarthakam . . 9
1.9.d:
सत्येव प्रमदाः काश्चिद्विशेषाधिगतागमाः ।
यत्तु शास्त्राधिकारित्वं वचनं स्यान्निरर्थकम् ॥ 9
1.9.m: Indeed, there are certain women who have acquired scripture in particular; / yet the statement that there is eligibility for sacred treatises would be without purpose [for all of them].

1.9.s:
kecidvedavido viprāḥ kṛtyairveṣakriyāparāḥ .
tathāpi 4 jātimātreṇa ta evātrādhikāriṇaḥ . . 1.9.10
1.9.d:
केचिद्वेदविदो विप्राः कृत्यैर्वेषक्रियापराः ।
तथापि 4 जातिमात्रेण त एवात्राधिकारिणः ॥ 1.9.10
1.9.m: Some brāhmaṇas who know the Veda are intent upon ritual actions in appearance only; / yet by caste alone, they indeed are eligible in this matter.

1.9.s:
kriyante vedaśāstrajñaiḥ prayogāḥ śāstralaukikāḥ .
sthitameṣāmadūre'pi śāstrameva nibandhanam . . 11
1.9.d:
क्रियन्ते वेदशास्त्रज्ञैः प्रयोगाः शास्त्रलौकिकाः ।
स्थितमेषामदूरेऽपि शास्त्रमेव निबन्धनम् ॥ 11
1.9.m: Rites of the sacred treatises and ordinary rites are performed by those who know the Veda and sacred texts; / even when not close to them, the sacred text alone remains their foundation.

1.9.s:
vyādhadhīvaragopālaprabhṛtīnāṃ ca dṛśyate .
viṣṭyaṃ gārakasauryādidinānāṃ parivarjanam . . 12
1.9.d:
व्याधधीवरगोपालप्रभृतीनां च दृश्यते ।
विष्ट्यं गारकसौर्यादिदिनानां परिवर्जनम् ॥ 12
1.9.m: And among hunters, fishermen, cowherds, and the like, / the avoidance of days such as [inauspicious] astrological periods, Tuesday, and Sunday is observed.

1.9.s:
gamyāgamyādikāryeyaṃ niyatācārasaṃsthitiḥ .
lokānāṃ śāstravākyānāṃ prāṇāḥ sveṣṭanibandhanāḥ .. 13
1.9.d:
गम्यागम्यादिकार्येयं नियताचारसंस्थितिः ।
लोकानां शास्त्रवाक्यानां प्राणाः स्वेष्टनिबन्धनाः ॥ 13
1.9.m: This established order of fixed conduct—actions permitted and forbidden, and the like— / has the words of sacred treatises as its life-breath, based on the desires of the people.

1.9.s:
tasmāccaturṇāṃ varṇānāmāśramāṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ .
mukhyagauṇādibhedānāṃ jñeyā śāstrādhikāritā . . 14
1.9.d:
तस्माच्चतुर्णां वर्णानामाश्रमाणां च सर्वशः ।
मुख्यगौणादिभेदानां ज्ञेया शास्त्राधिकारिता ॥ 14
1.9.m: Therefore, for the four classes and stages of life, in all respects, / eligibility for the sacred texts is to be known through distinctions such as primary and secondary.

1.9.s:
paurvāparyaṃ tu vijñātumaśakyaṃ lokaśāstrayoḥ .
tacchāstrameva mantavyaṃ yathā karmaśarīravat . . 15
1.9.d:
पौर्वापर्यं तु विज्ञातुमशक्यं लोकशास्त्रयोः ।
तच्छास्त्रमेव मन्तव्यं यथा कर्मशरीरवत् ॥ 15
1.9.m: It is impossible to know the priority or posteriority of the world and sacred texts; / it is to be understood that the sacred text is [related to the world] just as action is to the body.

1.9.s:
āgame ca purāṇe ca dvidhaiva nāstikagraham .
mārgaṃ mahadbhirācīrṇaṃ prapadyetāvikalpadhīḥ . . 16
1.9.d:
आगमे च पुराणे च द्विधैव नास्तिकग्रहम् ।
मार्गं महद्भिराचीर्णं प्रपद्येताविकल्पधीः ॥ 16
1.9.m: Regarding both scripture and the Purāṇa, [casting aside] the two kinds of atheistic grasp, / one should with resolute mind take up the path followed by the great.

1.9.s:
mūlaṃ gṛhasthadharmāṇāṃ yasmānnāryaḥ pativratāḥ .
tasmādāsāṃ pravakṣyāmi bharturārādhane vidhim . . 17
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārdhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi
āgamanapraśaṃsānāma navamo'dhyāyaḥ . 9 .
strīdurācāravarṇanam
1.9.d:
मूलं गृहस्थधर्माणां यस्मान्नार्यः पतिव्रताः ।
तस्मादासां प्रवक्ष्यामि भर्तुराराधने विधिम् ॥ 17
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि
आगमनप्रशंसानाम नवमोऽध्यायः । 9 ।
स्त्रीदुराचारवर्णनम्
1.9.m:
Since devoted wives are the foundation of the duties of a householder, / I shall therefore declare the rule for their worship of the husband.
Thus ends the ninth chapter, named “Praise of Scripture” in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty-thousand [verses].
Description of the Misconduct of Women

1.10.s:
brahmovāca
ārādhyānāṃ hi sarveṣāmayamārādhane vidhiḥ .
citta1 jñānānuvṛttiśca hitaiṣitvaṃ ca sarvadā . . 1
1.10.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
आराध्यानां हि सर्वेषामयमाराधने विधिः ।
चित्त1 ज्ञानानुवृत्तिश्च हितैषित्वं च सर्वदा ॥ 1
1.10.m:
Brahmā said:
This indeed is the rule for the worship of all who are to be worshipped: / knowledge and compliance with their mind, and always desiring their welfare.

1.10.s:
kanyā punarbhūrveśyā ca trividhā eva yoṣitaḥ .
priyā madhyāpriyā caiva yogyā madhyetarā tathā . . 2
1.10.d:
कन्या पुनर्भूर्वेश्या च त्रिविधा एव योषितः ।
प्रिया मध्याप्रिया चैव योग्या मध्येतरा तथा ॥ 2
1.10.m: Maidens, remarried women, and courtesans are indeed the three kinds of women; / and [they are] pleasant, middling, and unpleasant, as well as suitable and unsuitable.

1.10.s:
samā śreṣṭhā ca nīcā ca bhūyopi trividhāḥ punaḥ .
pūrvavatparayorvṛttiriṣṭānuktyā 1 priyāpriye . . 3
1.10.d:
समा श्रेष्ठा च नीचा च भूयोपि त्रिविधाः पुनः ।
पूर्ववत्परयोर्वृत्तिरिष्टानुक्त्या 1 प्रियाप्रिये ॥ 3
1.10.m: Equal, superior, and base—they are again threefold; / the conduct of the other two is as before, pleasant and unpleasant according to the mention of what is desired.

1.10.s:
adhamāpriyayoratra patipatnyādikā matā .
niṣiddhānāṃ tu bhakṣyādi taddhi yatnādvidhīyate . . 4
1.10.d:
अधमाप्रिययोरत्र पतिपत्न्यादिका मता ।
निषिद्धानां तु भक्ष्यादि तद्धि यत्नाद्विधीयते ॥ 4
1.10.m: Here, regarding the base and the unpleasant [women], the husband, wife, and others are considered; / for food and the like that is forbidden is prescribed [for them] with effort.

1.10.s:
ekadvitvabahutvādyā2 ye bhedāḥ samudāhṛtāḥ .
jyeṣṭhādivṛtte vakṣyāmastānaśeṣāndvijottamāḥ . . 5
1.10.d:
एकद्वित्वबहुत्वाद्या2 ये भेदाः समुदाहृताः ।
ज्येष्ठादिवृत्ते वक्ष्यामस्तानशेषान्द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 5
1.10.m: The distinctions mentioned, such as being one, two, or many, / all of them we shall declare in the conduct of the senior [wife] and others, O best of the twice-born.

1.10.s:
vṛttaṃ ca dvividhaṃ strīṇāṃ bāhyamābhyantaraṃ tathā .
bharturanyajane bāhyaṃ tasyāḥ śārīramāntaram . . 6
1.10.d:
वृत्तं च द्विविधं स्त्रीणां बाह्यमाभ्यन्तरं तथा ।
भर्तुरन्यजने बाह्यं तस्याः शारीरमान्तरम् ॥ 6
1.10.m:
And the conduct of women is of two kinds: external and internal.
The external relates to persons other than the husband; her internal conduct concerns bodily matters.

1.10.s:
jñātītaravibhāgena tadbāhyaṃ dvividhaṃ punaḥ .
pūjyaṃ tulyaṃ kaniṣṭhaṃ ca tatpratyekaṃ punastridhā . . 7
1.10.d:
ज्ञातीतरविभागेन तद्बाह्यं द्विविधं पुनः ।
पूज्यं तुल्यं कनिष्ठं च तत्प्रत्येकं पुनस्त्रिधा ॥ 7
1.10.m:
Through the division of relatives and non-relatives, that external [conduct] is again twofold.
That in turn is each threefold: toward superiors, equals, and inferiors.

1.10.s:
rahorataṃ prakāśaṃ ca śārīramapi tattridhā .
bhartuścittānukūlyena prayoktavyaṃ yathocitam . . 8
1.10.d:
रहोरतं प्रकाशं च शारीरमपि तत्त्रिधा ।
भर्तुश्चित्तानुकूल्येन प्रयोक्तव्यं यथोचितम् ॥ 8
1.10.m:
The bodily [conduct] too is threefold: in secret, in intercourse, and in public.
It should be employed appropriately, in accordance with the husband's wishes.

1.10.s:
mātā pitā svasā bhrātā pitṛvyācāryamātulāḥ .
sabhāryā 3 bhaginī bhartā bhartṛmātṛpitṛṣvasā . . 9
1.10.d:
माता पिता स्वसा भ्राता पितृव्याचार्यमातुलाः ।
सभार्या 3 भगिनी भर्ता भर्तृमातृपितृष्वसा ॥ 9
1.10.m:
Mother, father, sister, brother, paternal uncle, teacher, and maternal uncle,
together with his wife, sister, husband, and the husband's maternal and paternal aunts,

1.10.s:
dhātrī vṛddhāṅganādiśca yastatrāstā samo janaḥ .
prathamoḍhā sapatnī ca strīṇāṃ mānyatamo gaṇaḥ 4 . . 1.10.10
1.10.d:
धात्री वृद्धाङ्गनादिश्च यस्तत्रास्ता समो जनः ।
प्रथमोढा सपत्नी च स्त्रीणां मान्यतमो गणः 4 ॥ 1.10.10
1.10.m:
nurse, elderly women, and others—whatever person is equal among them;
and the co-wife married first: this is the group most worthy of honour for women.

1.10.s:
eṣāmeva tvapatyādibhaginībhrātarastathā .
kaniṣṭhā bharturityādibhāryāścāptasamo mataḥ . . 11
1.10.d:
एषामेव त्वपत्यादिभगिनीभ्रातरस्तथा ।
कनिष्ठा भर्तुरित्यादिभार्याश्चाप्तसमो मतः ॥ 11
1.10.m:
The children and other [descendants] of these very persons, as well as sisters and brothers,
and the husband's younger wives and so forth, are considered equal to trusted kin.

1.10.s:
hīno'nyaḥ śāsanīyastu tatra tāvanna vidyate .
yogyatā sutasaubhāgyairna yāvatsyātpratiṣṭhitā . . 12
1.10.d:
हीनोऽन्यः शासनीयस्तु तत्र तावन्न विद्यते ।
योग्यता सुतसौभाग्यैर्न यावत्स्यात्प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ 12
1.10.m:
Another who is inferior and fit to be commanded does not exist for her at that time,
so long as her competence is not established through sons and good fortune.

1.10.s:
yatrāpi guru bhartṝṇāmānukūlyena sarvadā .
vṛttiḥ praśasyate strīṇāṃ pūjācārāvirodhinī5 . . 13
1.10.d:
यत्रापि गुरु भर्तॄणामानुकूल्येन सर्वदा ।
वृत्तिः प्रशस्यते स्त्रीणां पूजाचाराविरोधिनी5 ॥ 13
1.10.m:
Even where [she is], the conduct of women in constant accordance
with the husband's elders, not conflicting with worship and customary rites, is praised.

1.10.s:
devaraiḥ patimitraiśca parihāsakriyocitaiḥ .
viviktadeśāvasthānaṃ varjayediti narma ca . . 14
1.10.d:
देवरैः पतिमित्रैश्च परिहासक्रियोचितैः ।
विविक्तदेशावस्थानं वर्जयेदिति नर्म च ॥ 14
1.10.m:
With brothers-in-law and the husband's friends who are prone to joking,
she should avoid staying in a secluded place, and likewise jesting.

1.10.s:
prāyaśo hi kulastrīṇāṃ śīlavidhvaṃsahetavaḥ .
duṣṭayogo raho nityaṃ svātantryamatinarmatā . . 15
1.10.d:
प्रायशो हि कुलस्त्रीणां शीलविध्वंसहेतवः ।
दुष्टयोगो रहो नित्यं स्वातन्त्र्यमतिनर्मता ॥ 15
1.10.m:
For these are generally the causes of the ruin of character in women of noble family:
association with corrupt people, constant privacy, independence, and excessive jesting.

1.10.s:
duṣṭasaṅge tvarā strīṇāṃ yuvabhirnarma nocitam .
nirbheṣatā svatantrāṇāṃ sāphalyaṃ rahasi yajet . . 16
1.10.d:
दुष्टसङ्गे त्वरा स्त्रीणां युवभिर्नर्म नोचितम् ।
निर्भेषता स्वतन्त्राणां साफल्यं रहसि यजेत् ॥ 16
1.10.m:
Eagerness for bad company is unsuited for women, as is jesting with young men.
Unrestraint belongs to independent women; one should abandon seeking fulfillment in secret.

1.10.s:
puṃso duṣṭeṅgitākārānduṣṭabhāvaprayojitān .
bhrātṛvatpitṛvaccaitānpaśyatī parivarjayet . . 17
1.10.d:
पुंसो दुष्टेङ्गिताकारान्दुष्टभावप्रयोजितान् ।
भ्रातृवत्पितृवच्चैतान्पश्यती परिवर्जयेत् ॥ 17
1.10.m:
Men who show corrupt gestures and expressions, driven by corrupt intent—
beholding them as like a brother or a father, she should avoid them.

1.10.s:
puṃso' nyāgrahamālāpasmitaviprekṣitāni ca .
karāntareṇa 1 dravyāṇāṃ nibandhaṃ grahaṇārpaṇam . . 18
1.10.d:
पुंसो' न्याग्रहमालापस्मितविप्रेक्षितानि च ।
करान्तरेण 1 द्रव्याणां निबन्धं ग्रहणार्पणम् ॥ 18
1.10.m:
Insistence upon men, conversation, smiling, and sideways glances toward them,
passing and receiving articles from hand to hand,

1.10.s:
dvārapradeśāvasthānaṃ rājamārgāvalokanam .
prekṣodyānādiśīlatvaṃ niruṣyāddeśamālayam . . 19
1.10.d:
द्वारप्रदेशावस्थानं राजमार्गावलोकनम् ।
प्रेक्षोद्यानादिशीलत्वं निरुष्याद्देशमालयम् ॥ 19
1.10.m:
standing at the doorway, gazing at the royal highway,
being fond of spectacles, gardens, and the like, and dwelling outside the region or house,

1.10.s:
bahūnāṃ darśane sthānaṃ dṛṣṭivākkāyacāpalam .
ṣṭhīvanatvaṃ sasītkāramuccairhasitajalpitam . . 1.10.20
1.10.d:
बहूनां दर्शने स्थानं दृष्टिवाक्कायचापलम् ।
ष्ठीवनत्वं ससीत्कारमुच्चैर्हसितजल्पितम् ॥ 1.10.20
1.10.m:
standing where many can see, restlessness of eyes, speech, and body,
spitting with a hissing sound, and loud laughing and chattering,

1.10.s:
sāṅgatyaṃ liṅgiduṣṭastrībhighṛṇīkṣaṇikādibhiḥ .
mantramaṇḍaladīkṣāyāṃ saktiḥ saṃvasaneṣu ca . . 21
1.10.d:
साङ्गत्यं लिङ्गिदुष्टस्त्रीभिघृणीक्षणिकादिभिः ।
मन्त्रमण्डलदीक्षायां सक्तिः संवसनेषु च ॥ 21
1.10.m:
association with mendicants, wicked women, female ascetics, fortune-tellers, and the like,
and attachment to initiation into mantras and maṇḍalas, and to dwelling together—

1.10.s:
ityevamādidurvṛttaṃ prāyoduṣṭajanocitam .
varjayetparirakṣantī kulatritayavācyatām . . 22
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi
strīdurvṛttavarṇanaṃnāma daśamo'dhyāyaḥ . 10 .
strīṇāṃ gṛhasthadharmavarṇanam
1.10.d:
इत्येवमादिदुर्वृत्तं प्रायोदुष्टजनोचितम् ।
वर्जयेत्परिरक्षन्ती कुलत्रितयवाच्यताम् ॥ 22
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि
स्त्रीदुर्वृत्तवर्णनंनाम दशमोऽध्यायः । 10 ।
स्त्रीणां गृहस्थधर्मवर्णनम्
1.10.m:
such bad conduct, generally suited for corrupt persons,
she should avoid, safeguarding the three families from reproach.
Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled “Description of the Bad Conduct of Women,” in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Householder Duties of Women

1.11.s:
brahmovāca
yā patiṃ daivataṃ paśyenmanovākkāyakarmabhiḥ .
taccharīrārdhajāteva sarvadā hitamācaret . . 1
1.11.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
या पतिं दैवतं पश्येन्मनोवाक्कायकर्मभिः ।
तच्छरीरार्धजातेव सर्वदा हितमाचरेत् ॥ 1
1.11.m:
Brahmā said:
She who regards her husband as a deity in thought, word, body, and deed,
as if born from half his body, should always act for his benefit.

1.11.s:
tatpriyāṃ priyavatpaśyettaddveṣyā dveṣyavatsadā .
adharmānarthayuktebhyo'yuktā cāsya nivartate . . 2
1.11.d:
तत्प्रियां प्रियवत्पश्येत्तद्द्वेष्या द्वेष्यवत्सदा ।
अधर्मानर्थयुक्तेभ्योऽयुक्ता चास्य निवर्तते ॥ 2
1.11.m:
What he holds dear, she should view as dear; what he hates, she should always view as hateful;
and if he is engaged in unrighteousness and harm, she, remaining uninvolved, dissuades him.

1.11.s:
priyaṃ kimasya kiṃ pathyaṃ sāmyaṃ cāsya kathaṃ bhavet .
jñātvaivaṃ sarvabhṛtyeṣu na pramādyeta vai dvijāḥ . . 3
1.11.d:
प्रियं किमस्य किं पथ्यं साम्यं चास्य कथं भवेत् ।
ज्ञात्वैवं सर्वभृत्येषु न प्रमाद्येत वै द्विजाः ॥ 3
1.11.m:
Knowing what is dear to him, what is wholesome, and how his balance may be kept,
she should never be negligent among all the servants, O twice-born!

1.11.s:
devatāpitṛkāryeṣu bhartuḥ snānāśanādiṣu .
satkāre'bhyāgatānāṃ ca yathaucityaṃ na hāpayet . . 4
1.11.d:
देवतापितृकार्येषु भर्तुः स्नानाशनादिषु ।
सत्कारेऽभ्यागतानां च यथौचित्यं न हापयेत् ॥ 4
1.11.m:
In rites for deities and ancestors, in the husband's bathing, eating, and other needs,
and in the hospitable reception of guests, she must not fail in what is proper.

1.11.s:
veśmātmā ca śarīraṃ hi gṛhiṇīnāṃ dvidhā kṛtam .
saṃskartavyaṃ prayatnena prathamaṃ paścimādapi . . 5
1.11.d:
वेश्मात्मा च शरीरं हि गृहिणीनां द्विधा कृतम् ।
संस्कर्तव्यं प्रयत्नेन प्रथमं पश्चिमादपि ॥ 5
1.11.m:
For the home and oneself, the body, are twofold for housewives;
the first should be carefully maintained even before the latter.

1.11.s:
kṛtvā veśma susaṃmṛṣṭaṃ trikālavihitārcanam .
vṛttakarmopabhogānāṃ saṃskartavyaṃ yathocitam . . 6
1.11.d:
कृत्वा वेश्म सुसंमृष्टं त्रिकालविहितार्चनम् ।
वृत्तकर्मोपभोगानां संस्कर्तव्यं यथोचितम् ॥ 6
1.11.m:
Having made the house thoroughly swept and clean, with worship performed at the three times of day,
she should arrange it properly for daily activities, chores, and use.

1.11.s:
prātarmadhyāparāhṇeṣu bahirmadhyāntareṣu ca .
gṛhasammārjanaṃ kṛtvā niṣkārānna niśi kṣipet . . 7
1.11.d:
प्रातर्मध्यापराह्णेषु बहिर्मध्यान्तरेषु च ।
गृहसम्मार्जनं कृत्वा निष्कारान्न निशि क्षिपेत् ॥ 7
1.11.m:
Having swept the house in the morning, midday, and afternoon,
outside, in the middle, and within, she should not throw the sweepings out at night.

1.11.s:
gomahiṣyādiśālānāṃ tatpurīṣādimātrakam .
vyapaneyaṃ tu yatnena sammārjanyā prasādhanam . . 8
1.11.d:
गोमहिष्यादिशालानां तत्पुरीषादिमात्रकम् ।
व्यपनेयं तु यत्नेन सम्मार्जन्या प्रसाधनम् ॥ 8
1.11.m:
From the stalls of cows, buffaloes, and other animals, all their dung and the like
must be removed with effort, and cleaning done with a broom.

1.11.s:
dāsakarmakarādīnāṃ bāhyābhyantaracāriṇām .
poṣaṇādividhiṃ vidyādanuṣṭhānaṃ ca karmasu . . 9
1.11.d:
दासकर्मकरादीनां बाह्याभ्यन्तरचारिणाम् ।
पोषणादिविधिं विद्यादनुष्ठानं च कर्मसु ॥ 9
1.11.m:
For male and female slaves and other servants who work outside and inside,
she should understand the rules of maintenance and their assignment to duties.

1.11.s:
śākamūlaphalādīnāṃ vallīnāmauṣadhasya ca .
saṅgrahaḥ sarvabījānāṃ yathākālaṃ yathābalam . . 1.11.10
1.11.d:
शाकमूलफलादीनां वल्लीनामौषधस्य च ।
सङ्ग्रहः सर्वबीजानां यथाकालं यथाबलम् ॥ 1.11.10
1.11.m:
The gathering of vegetables, roots, fruits, and the like, of creepers, medicine,
and of all kinds of seeds, should be done according to the season and one's capacity;

1.11.s:
tāmrakāṃsyāyasādīnāṃ kāṣṭhaveṇumayasya 1 ca .
mṛnmayānāṃ ca bhāṇḍānāṃ vividhānāṃ ca saṅgraham . . 11
1.11.d:
ताम्रकांस्यायसादीनां काष्ठवेणुमयस्य 1 च ।
मृन्मयानां च भाण्डानां विविधानां च सङ्ग्रहम् ॥ 11
1.11.m:
and the gathering of various vessels of copper, bell-metal, iron, and the like,
as well as those made of wood, bamboo, and clay;

1.11.s:
kuṇḍakādijaladroṇyā kalaśodañcatālukāḥ .
śākapātrāṇyanekāni snehānāṃ gorasasya ca . . 12
1.11.d:
कुण्डकादिजलद्रोण्या कलशोदञ्चतालुकाः ।
शाकपात्राण्यनेकानि स्नेहानां गोरसस्य च ॥ 12
1.11.m:
pots, water troughs, pitchers, water-drawing buckets, basins,
numerous vegetable-dishes, and vessels for oils and milk products;

1.11.s:
musalaṃ kuṇḍanīyaṃ tu yantrakaṃ2 cūrṇacālanī .
dohanyo netrakaṃ manthā maṇḍanyaḥ śṛṅkhalāni ca . . 13
1.11.d:
मुसलं कुण्डनीयं तु यन्त्रकं2 चूर्णचालनी ।
दोहन्यो नेत्रकं मन्था मण्डन्यः शृङ्खलानि च ॥ 13
1.11.m:
the pestle, the mortar, the millstone, the flour-sieve,
milking pails, churning ropes, churning sticks, decorations, and chains;

1.11.s:
saṃdaṃśaḥ kuṇḍikā śūlāḥ paṭṭapippalako dṛṣat .
ḍāvikā hastako darvī bhrāṣṭasphuṭalakāni ca . . 14
1.11.d:
संदंशः कुण्डिका शूलाः पट्टपिप्पलको दृषत् ।
डाविका हस्तको दर्वी भ्राष्टस्फुटलकानि च ॥ 14
1.11.m:
tongs, small pots, spits, wooden rollers, the grinding slab,
ladles, spoons, stirring paddles, frying pans, and platters;

1.11.s:
tulāprasthādimānāni mārjanyaḥ piṭakāni ca .
sarvametatprakurvīta prayatnena ca sarvadā . . 15
1.11.d:
तुलाप्रस्थादिमानानि मार्जन्यः पिटकानि च ।
सर्वमेतत्प्रकुर्वीत प्रयत्नेन च सर्वदा ॥ 15
1.11.m:
measuring balances, prastha-measures, brooms, and baskets—
she should always provide all these with care;

1.11.s:
hiṃgvādikamatho jājī pipalyo māricāni ca .
rājikā dhānyakaṃ śuṇṭhī tricaturjātakāni ca . . 16
1.11.d:
हिंग्वादिकमथो जाजी पिपल्यो मारिचानि च ।
राजिका धान्यकं शुण्ठी त्रिचतुर्जातकानि च ॥ 16
1.11.m:
also asafoetida and the like, cumin, long pepper, black pepper,
mustard, coriander, dry ginger, the three spices and the four spices;

1.11.s:
lavaṇaṃ kṣāravargāśca sauvīrakaparūṣakau .
dvidalāmalakaṃ ciṃcā sarvāśca snehajātayaḥ . . 17
1.11.d:
लवणं क्षारवर्गाश्च सौवीरकपरूषकौ ।
द्विदलामलकं चिंचा सर्वाश्च स्नेहजातयः ॥ 17
1.11.m:
salt, the alkali group, sour gruel, parūṣaka berries,
split pulses, myrobalan, tamarind, and all kinds of fats;

1.11.s:
śuṣkakāṣṭhāni vallūramariṣṭā piṣṭamāṣayoḥ .
vikārāḥ payasaścāpi vividhāḥ kandajātayaḥ . . 18
1.11.d:
शुष्ककाष्ठानि वल्लूरमरिष्टा पिष्टमाषयोः ।
विकाराः पयसश्चापि विविधाः कन्दजातयः ॥ 18
1.11.m:
dry wood, dried meat, dried fruits, cakes of ground flour and black gram,
various preparations of milk, and varieties of tubers.

1.11.s:
nityanaimittikānāṃ hi kāryāṇāmupayogataḥ .
sarvamityādi saṃgrāhyaṃ yathāvadvibhavocitam . . 19
1.11.d:
नित्यनैमित्तिकानां हि कार्याणामुपयोगतः ।
सर्वमित्यादि संग्राह्यं यथावद्विभवोचितम् ॥ 19
1.11.m:
For their use in daily and occasional rites and duties,
all such things should be properly collected in accordance with one's wealth.

1.11.s:
yatkāryāṇāṃ samutpattāvupāhartuṃ na dṛśyate .
tatprāgeva yathāyogaṃ saṅgṛhṇīyātprayatnataḥ . . 1.11.20
1.11.d:
यत्कार्याणां समुत्पत्तावुपाहर्तुं न दृश्यते ।
तत्प्रागेव यथायोगं सङ्गृह्णीयात्प्रयत्नतः ॥ 1.11.20
1.11.m:
Whatever cannot be easily obtained when tasks arise,
that she should gather carefully beforehand, in the proper manner.

1.11.s:
dhānyānāṃ ghṛṣṭapiṣṭānāṃ kṣuṇṇopahatayorapi .
bhṛśaṃ śuṣkārdrasiddhānāṃ kṣayavṛddhī nirūpayet . . 21
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi
gṛhadharmavarṇanaṃ nāmaikādaśo'dhyāyaḥ . 11 .
strīdharmavarṇanam
1.11.d:
धान्यानां घृष्टपिष्टानां क्षुण्णोपहतयोरपि ।
भृशं शुष्कार्द्रसिद्धानां क्षयवृद्धी निरूपयेत् ॥ 21
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि
गृहधर्मवर्णनं नामैकादशोऽध्यायः । 11 ।
स्त्रीधर्मवर्णनम्
1.11.m:
She should determine the decrease and increase of grains when rubbed, ground,
pounded, and husked, or thoroughly dried, moistened, and cooked.
Thus ends the eleventh chapter, titled “Description of Domestic Duties,” in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Duties of Women

1.12.s:
brahmovāca
vrīhīṇāṃ kodravāṇāṃ ca sāradharmamudārakaḥ 1 .
kaṅgukodravayorjñeyo varaṭaḥ pañcabhāgakaḥ . . 1
1.12.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
व्रीहीणां कोद्रवाणां च सारधर्ममुदारकः 1 ।
कङ्गुकोद्रवयोर्ज्ञेयो वरटः पञ्चभागकः ॥ 1

1.12.s:
pañcabhāgānpriyaṅgūnāṃ śālīnāṃ ca trayo'ṣṭa ca .
caṇakānāṃ tṛtīyāṃśaḥ samakṣuṇṇaṃ trayaṃ viduḥ . . 2
1.12.d:
पञ्चभागान्प्रियङ्गूनां शालीनां च त्रयोऽष्ट च ।
चणकानां तृतीयांशः समक्षुण्णं त्रयं विदुः ॥ 2
1.12.m:
Of Italian millet, five parts, and of winter rice, three and eight parts;
one-third of chickpeas: when evenly pounded, they know these three [ratios].

1.12.s:
pānīyayavagodhūmaṃ2 piṣṭadhānyacatuṣṭayam .
tulyamevāvagantavyaṃ mudgā māṣāstilā yavāḥ . . 3
1.12.d:
पानीययवगोधूमं2 पिष्टधान्यचतुष्टयम् ।
तुल्यमेवावगन्तव्यं मुद्गा माषास्तिला यवाः ॥ 3
1.12.m:
Water-barley and wheat, the four ground grains—
mung beans, black gram, sesame seeds, and barley—are to be understood as equal.

1.12.s:
pañcabhāgādikā ghṛṣṭā godhūmāḥ saktavastathā .
kulmāṣāḥ piṣṭamāṃsaṃ ca samyagardhādikaṃ bhavet . . 4
1.12.d:
पञ्चभागादिका घृष्टा गोधूमाः सक्तवस्तथा ।
कुल्माषाः पिष्टमांसं च सम्यगर्धादिकं भवेत् ॥ 4
1.12.m:
Wheat crushed by one-fifth part, and likewise groats,
boiled pulses, and minced meat become fully increased by half and more.

1.12.s:
siddhaṃ tadeva dviguṇaṃ punnāko yāvakastathā .
kaṅgukodravayorannaṃ caṇakodārakasya ca . . 5
1.12.d:
सिद्धं तदेव द्विगुणं पुन्नाको यावकस्तथा ।
कङ्गुकोद्रवयोरन्नं चणकोदारकस्य च ॥ 5
1.12.m:
When cooked, that same becomes doubled, as does punnāka and barley gruel,
and the cooked food of panic-seed, kodrava, chickpeas, and udāraka.

1.12.s:
dviguṇaṃ 4 cīnakānāṃ ca vrīhīṇāṃ ca caturguṇam .
śāleḥ pañcaguṇaṃ vidyātpurāṇe tvatiricyate . . 6
1.12.d:
द्विगुणं 4 चीनकानां च व्रीहीणां च चतुर्गुणम् ।
शालेः पञ्चगुणं विद्यात्पुराणे त्वतिरिच्यते ॥ 6
1.12.m: Twice [as much] for cīnaka grains, and fourfold for vrīhi rice; / one should know it to be fivefold for śāli rice, but in old grain it increases even more.

1.12.s:
kriyāpākaviśeṣāstu vṛddhirevopadiśyate .
nimittasya varānnasya tadvṛddhirdviguṇā bhavet . . 7
1.12.d:
क्रियापाकविशेषास्तु वृद्धिरेवोपदिश्यते ।
निमित्तस्य वरान्नस्य तद्वृद्धिर्द्विगुणा भवेत् ॥ 7
1.12.m: Increase is indeed taught according to particular modes of cooking; / the increase of choice food prepared for a special occasion becomes twofold.

1.12.s:
tasmādbhūyo virūḍhasya caturbhāgo vivardhate .
lājā dhānāḥ kalāyāśca bhṛṣṭāddviguṇavṛddhayaḥ . . 8
1.12.d:
तस्माद्भूयो विरूढस्य चतुर्भागो विवर्धते ।
लाजा धानाः कलायाश्च भृष्टाद्द्विगुणवृद्धयः ॥ 8
1.12.m: From that, [grain] that has sprouted further increases by a fourth; / puffed grain, parched grain, and peas increase twofold from roasting.

1.12.s:
bhraṣṭavyānāmato'nyeṣāṃ pañcabhāgo'dhiko mataḥ .
cāpakānāṃ ca piṣṭānāṃ pādahīnāḥ kalāyajāḥ . . 9
1.12.d:
भ्रष्टव्यानामतोऽन्येषां पञ्चभागोऽधिको मतः ।
चापकानां च पिष्टानां पादहीनाः कलायजाः ॥ 9
1.12.m: Of other grains to be roasted, an increase of one-fifth is considered proper; / and for flour-pastes, those made of peas are reduced by a quarter.

1.12.s:
mudgamāṣamasūrāṇāmardhapādāvarobhavet .
klinnaśuṣkavarānnānāṃ hānirvṛddhirviśiṣyate . . 1.12.10
1.12.d:
मुद्गमाषमसूराणामर्धपादावरोभवेत् ।
क्लिन्नशुष्कवरान्नानां हानिर्वृद्धिर्विशिष्यते ॥ 1.12.10
1.12.m: For mudga, māṣa, and lentils, it is lower by half a quarter; / loss and gain vary among moist, dry, and choice foods.

1.12.s:
tayārdhena tu śodhyānāmāḍhakyā mudgamāṣayoḥ .
masūrāṇāṃ ca jānīyātkṣayaṃ pañcamabhāgakam . . 11
1.12.d:
तयार्धेन तु शोध्यानामाढक्या मुद्गमाषयोः ।
मसूराणां च जानीयात्क्षयं पञ्चमभागकम् ॥ 11
1.12.m: Of those to be cleaned with half that [process], one should know / a loss of one-fifth for āḍhakī, mudga, māṣa, and lentils.

1.12.s:
ṣaḍbhāgenātasītailaṃ siddhārthakakapitthayoḥ .
tathā nimbakadambādau 1 vidyātpañcamabhāgakam . . 12
1.12.d:
षड्भागेनातसीतैलं सिद्धार्थककपित्थयोः ।
तथा निम्बकदम्बादौ 1 विद्यात्पञ्चमभागकम् ॥ 12
1.12.m: Linseed oil yields one-sixth; for white mustard and kapittha, / as well as for nimba, kadamba, and the like, one should know it yields one-fifth.

1.12.s:
tileṅgudīmadhūkānāṃ 2 naktamālakusumbhayoḥ .
jānīyātpādakaṃ tailaṃ khalamanyatpracakṣate . . 13
1.12.d:
तिलेङ्गुदीमधूकानां 2 नक्तमालकुसुम्भयोः ।
जानीयात्पादकं तैलं खलमन्यत्प्रचक्षते ॥ 13
1.12.m: One should know that sesamum, ingudī, madhūka, / naktamāla, and kusumbha yield a fourth in oil; what is left over they call oil-cake.

1.12.s:
kṣetrakālakriyādibhyaḥ kṣayādervyabhicārataḥ .
pratyakṣīkṛtya tānsamyaganumityāvadhārayet . . 14
1.12.d:
क्षेत्रकालक्रियादिभ्यः क्षयादेर्व्यभिचारतः ।
प्रत्यक्षीकृत्य तान्सम्यगनुमित्यावधारयेत् ॥ 14
1.12.m: Because variation [occurs] in loss and the like depending on field, season, preparation, and so forth, / one should ascertain them properly by inference after observing them directly.

1.12.s:
kṣīradoṣe gavāṃ 3 prasthaṃ mahiṣīṇāṃ ca sarpiṣaḥ .
pādādhikamajāvīnāmutpādaṃ tadvido viduḥ . . 15
1.12.d:
क्षीरदोषे गवां 3 प्रस्थं महिषीणां च सर्पिषः ।
पादाधिकमजावीनामुत्पादं तद्विदो विदुः ॥ 15
1.12.m: In the milking of cows, those who know it know the yield / to be a prastha of clarified butter, and for buffaloes, goats, and sheep, a fourth more.

1.12.s:
subhūmitṛṇakālebhyo vṛddhirvā kṣīrasarpiṣām .
atasteṣāṃ vidhātavyo hyarthādeva 4 viniścayaḥ . . 16
1.12.d:
सुभूमितृणकालेभ्यो वृद्धिर्वा क्षीरसर्पिषाम् ।
अतस्तेषां विधातव्यो ह्यर्थादेव 4 विनिश्चयः ॥ 16
1.12.m: Or an increase of milk and clarified butter comes from good land, grass, and seasons; / therefore, their determination must be made directly according to the actual fact.

1.12.s:
pratyakṣīkṛtya yatnena pakṣamāsāntare tathā .
payorvṛttairgavādīnāṃ kuryātsambhavanirṇayam . . 17
1.12.d:
प्रत्यक्षीकृत्य यत्नेन पक्षमासान्तरे तथा ।
पयोर्वृत्तैर्गवादीनां कुर्यात्सम्भवनिर्णयम् ॥ 17
1.12.m: Having observed carefully over the course of a fortnight or a month / through the milk-yields of cows and the like, one should make a determination of the possible [produce].

1.12.s:
kārpāsa kṛmikośaumaurṇaka kṣaumādikartanam .
kuṇipaṅgvandhayoṣābhirvidhavābhiśca kārayet . . 18
1.12.d:
कार्पास कृमिकोशौमौर्णक क्षौमादिकर्तनम् ।
कुणिपङ्ग्वन्धयोषाभिर्विधवाभिश्च कारयेत् ॥ 18
1.12.m: One should have the spinning of cotton, silkworm cocoons, wool, / linen, and the like done by crippled, lame, or blind women, and by widows.

1.12.s:
bālavṛddhāndhakārpaṇye yatkartavyamavaśyataḥ .
viniyogaṃ nayetsarvaṃ priyopagrahapūrvakam . . 19
1.12.d:
बालवृद्धान्धकार्पण्ये यत्कर्तव्यमवश्यतः ।
विनियोगं नयेत्सर्वं प्रियोपग्रहपूर्वकम् ॥ 19
1.12.m: Whatever must necessarily be done for the helpless, children, the elderly, and the blind, / one should direct all such employment preceded by affectionate assistance.

1.12.s:
karmaṇāmantarāleṣu proṣite cāpi bhartari .
svayaṃ vai tadanuṣṭheyaṃ nityānāṃ cāvirodhataḥ . . 1.12.20
1.12.d:
कर्मणामन्तरालेषु प्रोषिते चापि भर्तरि ।
स्वयं वै तदनुष्ठेयं नित्यानां चाविरोधतः ॥ 1.12.20
1.12.m: In the intervals between duties, and even when the husband has gone abroad, / [a wife] should herself attend to that, without conflict with the daily [chores].

1.12.s:
śūdrāṇāṃ sthūlasūkṣmatvaṃ bahutvaṃ ca vyayāvyayau .
matvā viśeṣaṃ kurvīta cetanapratipattiṣu . . 21
1.12.d:
शूद्राणां स्थूलसूक्ष्मत्वं बहुत्वं च व्ययाव्ययौ ।
मत्वा विशेषं कुर्वीत चेतनप्रतिपत्तिषु ॥ 21
1.12.m: Considering the coarseness, fineness, and abundance of [the work of] Śūdras, / as well as expense and non-expense, one should make distinctions in the allocation of wages.

1.12.s:
kārayedvastradhānyādi svāptavṛddhairadhiṣṭhitam 1 .
śūdrāṇāṃ kṣayavṛddhyādi mantavyaṃ vetanāni ca . . 22
1.12.d:
कारयेद्वस्त्रधान्यादि स्वाप्तवृद्धैरधिष्ठितम् 1 ।
शूद्राणां क्षयवृद्ध्यादि मन्तव्यं वेतनानि च ॥ 22
1.12.m: One should have cloth, grain, and the like supervised by trusted elders; / the loss, gain, and so forth, as well as the wages of the Śūdras, are to be assessed.

1.12.s:
kṣaumakārpāsayorvidyātsūtraṃ pañcamabhāgakam .
deśakālādibhāgāttu pratyakṣādeva nirṇayaḥ . . 23
1.12.d:
क्षौमकार्पासयोर्विद्यात्सूत्रं पञ्चमभागकम् ।
देशकालादिभागात्तु प्रत्यक्षादेव निर्णयः ॥ 23
1.12.m: One should know that thread [yields] one-fifth from flax and cotton; / but from variations of region, season, and so on, determination is made by direct observation alone.

1.12.s:
avaghātena tūlasya kṣayo viṃśatibhāgakaḥ .
channāṃ vyāptāṃ tu vātena tadvadūrṇāṃ pracakṣate . . 24
1.12.d:
अवघातेन तूलस्य क्षयो विंशतिभागकः ।
छन्नां व्याप्तां तु वातेन तद्वदूर्णां प्रचक्षते ॥ 24
1.12.m: By beating, the loss of cotton is one-twentieth; / they declare the same for wool that has been covered and penetrated by wind.

1.12.s:
pañcāśadbhāgikīṃ hāniṃ sūtre kurvīta lakṣaṇāt2 .
vṛddhistu maṇḍasamparkāddaśakādaśikā bhavet . . 25
1.12.d:
पञ्चाशद्भागिकीं हानिं सूत्रे कुर्वीत लक्षणात्2 ।
वृद्धिस्तु मण्डसम्पर्काद्दशकादशिका भवेत् ॥ 25
1.12.m: One should reckon a loss of one-fiftieth in thread according to standard rule; / but an increase of one-eleventh occurs from contact with starch.

1.12.s:
ślakṣṇamadhyamasūtrāṇāmardhādhikasamaṃ bhavet .
sthūlānāṃ tu punarmūlyātpādonaṃ bālacetanam . . 26
1.12.d:
श्लक्ष्णमध्यमसूत्राणामर्धाधिकसमं भवेत् ।
स्थूलानां तु पुनर्मूल्यात्पादोनं बालचेतनम् ॥ 26
1.12.m: For fine and medium threads, [the wage] should be equal [to the weight] plus a half; / but for coarse ones, the hair-spinning wage is a quarter less than the value.

1.12.s:
karmaṇo bhūribhedatvāddeśakālaprabhedataḥ .
tadvidbhya eva boddhavyo bālacetananiścayaḥ . . 27
1.12.d:
कर्मणो भूरिभेदत्वाद्देशकालप्रभेदतः ।
तद्विद्भ्य एव बोद्धव्यो बालचेतननिश्चयः ॥ 27
1.12.m: Because of the manifold divisions of work and the differences of place and time, / the determination of the hair-spinning wage should be learned only from experts.

1.12.s:
sthūlaṃ dinatrayaṃ deyaṃ madhyamaṃ ca trirātrikam .
sūkṣmamāpakṣato mṛṣṭaṃ 4 māsāttatparikarmakam . .
yadatra kṣatravṛddhyādi tadutsargātpradarśitam . . 28
1.12.d:
स्थूलं दिनत्रयं देयं मध्यमं च त्रिरात्रिकम् ।
सूक्ष्ममापक्षतो मृष्टं 4 मासात्तत्परिकर्मकम् ॥
यदत्र क्षत्रवृद्ध्यादि तदुत्सर्गात्प्रदर्शितम् ॥ 28
1.12.m: Three days are to be allowed for coarse [work], and three nights for medium; / fine cleaned [work] requires up to half a month, and elaborate finishing [up to] a month. / Whatever loss, increase, and the like is mentioned here has been shown as a general rule;

1.12.s:
kālakartrādibhedena vyabhicāro'pi dṛśyate .
śayyāsanānyanekāni kambalāścaturāśrikāḥ . . 29
1.12.d:
कालकर्त्रादिभेदेन व्यभिचारोऽपि दृश्यते ।
शय्यासनान्यनेकानि कम्बलाश्चतुराश्रिकाः ॥ 29
1.12.m: variation is also seen according to differences of time, worker, and the like. / Many beds and seats, and four-cornered blankets,

1.12.s:
kambukāścāvakoṣāśca madhyā raktāśca bhūriśaḥ .
gurubālādivṛddhānāmabhyāgatajanasya ca . . 1.12.30
1.12.d:
कम्बुकाश्चावकोषाश्च मध्या रक्ताश्च भूरिशः ।
गुरुबालादिवृद्धानामभ्यागतजनस्य च ॥ 1.12.30
1.12.m: kambuka cloths, avakośa cloths, medium and red ones in abundance, / for elders, children, old people, and visiting guests,

1.12.s:
bhogāyānugato bharttā kuryādvividhamātrakam .
yadasya śvaśurādīnāṃ kalpitaṃ śayanādikam . . 31
1.12.d:
भोगायानुगतो भर्त्ता कुर्याद्विविधमात्रकम् ।
यदस्य श्वशुरादीनां कल्पितं शयनादिकम् ॥ 31
1.12.m: a devoted husband should make of various kinds for their enjoyment. / Whatever bedding and the like has been arranged for his father-in-law and others,

1.12.s:
bhartuścaiva viśeṣaṇa tadanyena na kārayet .
vastraṃ mālyamalaṅkāraṃ vidhṛtaṃ devarādibhiḥ . . 32
1.12.d:
भर्तुश्चैव विशेषण तदन्येन न कारयेत् ।
वस्त्रं माल्यमलङ्कारं विधृतं देवरादिभिः ॥ 32
1.12.m: and especially for her husband, [the wife] must not have used by anyone else. / Garments, garlands, or ornaments worn by brothers-in-law and the like,

1.12.s:
na dhārayenna caiteṣāmākramecchayanāni vā .
piṇyākanakakuṭṭāśca 3 kālarūkṣāṇi yāni ca . . 33
1.12.d:
न धारयेन्न चैतेषामाक्रमेच्छयनानि वा ।
पिण्याकनककुट्टाश्च 3 कालरूक्षाणि यानि च ॥ 33
1.12.m: she should not wear, nor should she step onto their beds. / Oil-cakes, pestle-crushed grains, and whatever has become dry over time,

1.12.s:
heyaṃ paryuṣitādyannaṃ gobhaktenopayojayet .
kulānāṃ bahudhenūnāṃ godhyakṣavrajajīvinām . . 34
1.12.d:
हेयं पर्युषिताद्यन्नं गोभक्तेनोपयोजयेत् ।
कुलानां बहुधेनूनां गोध्यक्षव्रजजीविनाम् ॥ 34
1.12.m: stale food, and other things to be discarded should be used as feed for cows. / For families with many milk-cows who live by pastures supervised by a cowherd,

1.12.s:
kilāṭagavikādīnāṃ bhaktārthamupayojanam .
dadhnaḥ samāharetsarpirduhedvatsānna pīḍayet . . 35
1.12.d:
किलाटगविकादीनां भक्तार्थमुपयोजनम् ।
दध्नः समाहरेत्सर्पिर्दुहेद्वत्सान्न पीडयेत् ॥ 35
1.12.m: curds, cow-produce, and the like are used for food. / One should collect clarified butter from yoghurt; one should milk [the cows but] not distress the calves.

1.12.s:
varṣāśaradvasanteṣu dvau kālāvanyadā sakṛt .
takraṃ vāpyupayuñjīta śvavarāhādipoṣaṇe . . 36
1.12.d:
वर्षाशरद्वसन्तेषु द्वौ कालावन्यदा सकृत् ।
तक्रं वाप्युपयुञ्जीत श्ववराहादिपोषणे ॥ 36
1.12.m: In the rains, autumn, and spring, [milking is done] twice a day, at other times once. / One may also use buttermilk to nourish dogs, pigs, and the like,

1.12.s:
piṇyākakledanārthaṃ vā vikreyaṃ vā tadarhayet .
vṛttiṃ dhānyahiraṇyena gopādīnāṃ prakalpayet . . 3 7
te hi kṣīravratā lobhādupahanyustadanvayān .
dohakālaṃ gavāṃ dogdhānītivarteta vai dvijāḥ . . 38
1.12.d:
पिण्याकक्लेदनार्थं वा विक्रेयं वा तदर्हयेत् ।
वृत्तिं धान्यहिरण्येन गोपादीनां प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 3 7
ते हि क्षीरव्रता लोभादुपहन्युस्तदन्वयान् ।
दोहकालं गवां दोग्धानीतिवर्तेत वै द्विजाः ॥ 38
1.12.m: or for moistening oil-cake, or one may consider it suitable for sale. / One should arrange the livelihood of cowherds and others with grain and gold; / for, bound to milk, out of greed they might harm their offspring. / The milkers should not exceed the milking-time of the cows, O twice-born ones.

1.12.s:
prasarodakayorgopā manthakasya ca manthakāḥ .
māsamekaṃ yathā stanyaṃ māsamekaṃ stanadvayam . . 39
1.12.d:
प्रसरोदकयोर्गोपा मन्थकस्य च मन्थकाः ।
मासमेकं यथा स्तन्यं मासमेकं स्तनद्वयम् ॥ 39
1.12.m: There should be cowherds for flowing water and churners for the churn. / For one month, as [prescribed], [the calf receives] one teat, for one month two teats;

1.12.s:
satataṃ pāyayedūrdhvaṃ stanamekaṃ stanadvayam .
tilapiṣṭābhiḥ piṇḍābhistṛṇena lavaṇena ca . .
vāriṇā ca yathākālaṃ puṣṇīyāditi vatsakān . .1.12.4 0
jaradgurgarbhiṇī dhenurvatsā vatsatarī tathā .
pañcānāṃ samabhāgena ghāsaṃ yūthe prakalpayet . . 41
1.12.d:
सततं पाययेदूर्ध्वं स्तनमेकं स्तनद्वयम् ।
तिलपिष्टाभिः पिण्डाभिस्तृणेन लवणेन च ॥
वारिणा च यथाकालं पुष्णीयादिति वत्सकान् ॥1.12.4 0
जरद्गुर्गर्भिणी धेनुर्वत्सा वत्सतरी तथा ।
पञ्चानां समभागेन घासं यूथे प्रकल्पयेत् ॥ 41
1.12.m: thereafter, one should continually let it drink from one teat or two teats. / With balls of ground sesamum, with grass, with salt, / and with water at the proper time, one should thus nourish the calves. / An old cow, a pregnant cow, a milch-cow, a calf, and a heifer— / one should arrange fodder in equal parts among these five in the herd.

1.12.s:
eko gopālakastasya trayāṇāmatha vā dvayam .
pañcānāṃ vatsakaścaikaḥ pravarāstu pṛthakpṛthak . . 42
1.12.d:
एको गोपालकस्तस्य त्रयाणामथ वा द्वयम् ।
पञ्चानां वत्सकश्चैकः प्रवरास्तु पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 42
1.12.m: There should be one cowherd for that [herd], or two for three [herds]; / and for five [cows] there should be one calf; the best [animals], however, [are tended] separately.

1.12.s:
gocarasyānayanārthaṃ vyālānāṃ trāsanāya 1 ca .
ghaṇṭā karṇeṣu badhnīyuḥ śobhārakṣārthameva ca . . 43
1.12.d:
गोचरस्यानयनार्थं व्यालानां त्रासनाय 1 च ।
घण्टा कर्णेषु बध्नीयुः शोभारक्षार्थमेव च ॥ 43
1.12.m: To bring them to pasture, to frighten wild beasts, / and for decoration and protection, they should tie bells to their ears.

1.12.s:
paśavye vyālanirmukte deśe bhūritṛṇodake .
abhūtaduṣṭe vāraṇye sadā kurvīta gokulam . . 44
1.12.d:
पशव्ये व्यालनिर्मुक्ते देशे भूरितृणोदके ।
अभूतदुष्टे वारण्ये सदा कुर्वीत गोकुलम् ॥ 44
1.12.m: In a region wholesome for cattle, free of wild beasts, with abundant grass and water, / and in a forest not afflicted by evil spirits, one should always establish a cattle-station.

1.12.s:
saguptamaṭavīvāsaṃ nityaṃ kuryādajāvikam .
ūrṇāṃ varṣe dvirādadyāccaitrāśvayujamāsayoḥ . . 45
1.12.d:
सगुप्तमटवीवासं नित्यं कुर्यादजाविकम् ।
ऊर्णां वर्षे द्विरादद्याच्चैत्राश्वयुजमासयोः ॥ 45
1.12.m: One should always keep the dwelling of goats and sheep guarded in the forest. / One should shear the wool twice a year, in the months of Caitra and Āśvayuja.

1.12.s:
yūthe mṛṣā daśaitāsāṃ catvāraḥ pañca vā gavām .
aśvoṣṭramahiṣāṇāṃ ca yathā syuḥ sukhasevitāḥ . . 56
1.12.d:
यूथे मृषा दशैतासां चत्वारः पञ्च वा गवाम् ।
अश्वोष्ट्रमहिषाणां च यथा स्युः सुखसेविताः ॥ 56
1.12.m: In a herd of these [sheep and goats], ten [males are suitable], or four or five for cows, / and for horses, camels, and buffaloes, so that they may live comfortably.

1.12.s:
vidyātkṛṣīvalādīnā yogaṃ kṛṣikakarmasu .
bhaktavetanalābhaṃ ca karmakālānurūpataḥ . . 47
1.12.d:
विद्यात्कृषीवलादीना योगं कृषिककर्मसु ।
भक्तवेतनलाभं च कर्मकालानुरूपतः ॥ 47
1.12.m: One should know the engagement of farmers and the like in agricultural tasks, / as well as the provision of food and wages according to the work and the season.

1.12.s:
kṣetrakedāravāṭeṣu bhṛtyānāṃ karma kurvatām .
khaleṣu ca vijānīyātkriyāyogaṃ pratikṣaṇam . . 48
1.12.d:
क्षेत्रकेदारवाटेषु भृत्यानां कर्म कुर्वताम् ।
खलेषु च विजानीयात्क्रियायोगं प्रतिक्षणम् ॥ 48
1.12.m: For servants doing work in open fields, rice-plots, gardens, / and threshing-floors, one should supervise the application of labour at every moment.

1.12.s:
yogyatātiśayaṃ matvā karmayogeṣu kasyacit .
grāsācchadaśirobhyaṅgairviśeṣaṃ tasya kārayet . . 49
1.12.d:
योग्यतातिशयं मत्वा कर्मयोगेषु कस्यचित् ।
ग्रासाच्छदशिरोभ्यङ्गैर्विशेषं तस्य कारयेत् ॥ 49
1.12.m: Recognising an exceptional competence in someone regarding work-assignments, / one should grant him special treatment with food, clothing, and head-anointings.

1.12.s:
padmaśākādivāpānāṃ kandabījādijanmanām .
saṅgrahaḥ sarvabījānāṃ kāle vāpaḥ subhūmiṣu . . 1.12.50
1.12.d:
पद्मशाकादिवापानां कन्दबीजादिजन्मनाम् ।
सङ्ग्रहः सर्वबीजानां काले वापः सुभूमिषु ॥ 1.12.50
1.12.m: For plantings of lotuses, vegetables, and the like, and those born from tubers, seeds, and so forth, / there should be a collection of all seeds and sowing at the proper time in good soils.

1.12.s:
jātānāṃ rakṣaṇaṃ samyagrakṣitānāṃ ca saṃgrahaḥ .
teṣāṃ ca saṃgṛhītānāṃ yathāvannivapakriyā . . 51
1.12.d:
जातानां रक्षणं सम्यग्रक्षितानां च संग्रहः ।
तेषां च संगृहीतानां यथावन्निवपक्रिया ॥ 51
1.12.m: The proper protection of those that have sprouted, the harvesting of those preserved, / and of those harvested, their proper sowing in season;

1.12.s:
gṛhamūlaṃ striyaścaiva dhānyamūlo gṛhāśramaḥ .
tasmāddhānyeṣu bhakteṣu na kuryānmuktahastatām . . 52
1.12.d:
गृहमूलं स्त्रियश्चैव धान्यमूलो गृहाश्रमः ।
तस्माद्धान्येषु भक्तेषु न कुर्यान्मुक्तहस्तताम् ॥ 52
1.12.m: women are the root of the household, and the householder's stage of life is rooted in grain. / Therefore, one should not be lavish with grains and cooked food.

1.12.s:
dhānyaṃ tu sañcitaṃ nityaṃ mito bhaktaparivyayaḥ .
na cānte muktahastatvaṃ gṛhiṇīnāṃ praśasyate . . 53
1.12.d:
धान्यं तु सञ्चितं नित्यं मितो भक्तपरिव्ययः ।
न चान्ते मुक्तहस्तत्वं गृहिणीनां प्रशस्यते ॥ 53
1.12.m: Grain should always be accumulated, the consumption of cooked food measured; / nor is lavishness ever praised in housewives.

1.12.s:
alpamityeva nāvajñāṃ caredanneṣu vai dvijāḥ .
madhuvalmīkayorvṛddhiṃ kṣayaṃ dṛṣṭvāṃjanasya ca . . 54
1.12.d:
अल्पमित्येव नावज्ञां चरेदन्नेषु वै द्विजाः ।
मधुवल्मीकयोर्वृद्धिं क्षयं दृष्ट्वांजनस्य च ॥ 54
1.12.m: O twice-born, one should not disregard food simply thinking, 'It is small,' / seeing the increase of honey and anthills, and the dwindling of eye-salve.

1.12.s:
ye kecidiha nirdiṣṭā vyāpārāḥ puruṣocitāḥ .
dāmpatyoraikyamāsthāya taddhidānaprasaṅgataḥ . . 55
1.12.d:
ये केचिदिह निर्दिष्टा व्यापाराः पुरुषोचिताः ।
दाम्पत्योरैक्यमास्थाय तद्धिदानप्रसङ्गतः ॥ 55
1.12.m: Whatever tasks suitable for men have been mentioned here, / resting upon the unity of husband and wife, are applied accordingly through their union.

1.12.s:
santyeva puruṣā loke strīpradhānāḥ sahasraśaḥ .
teṣu tāsāṃ prayoktṛtvādadoṣa iti gṛhyatām . . 56
1.12.d:
सन्त्येव पुरुषा लोके स्त्रीप्रधानाः सहस्रशः ।
तेषु तासां प्रयोक्तृत्वाददोष इति गृह्यताम् ॥ 56
1.12.m: There are indeed thousands of men in the world who are led by their wives; / since wives direct them, let it be understood as free of fault.

1.12.s:
evaṃ yogyatayā yuktā saubhāgyenodyamena ca .
samyagārādhya bhartāraṃ tatrainaṃ vaśamānayet . . 57
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhmaṇe parvaṇi strīdharmavarṇanaṃ
nāma dvādaśo'dhyāya . 12
strīdharmavarṇanam
1.12.d:
एवं योग्यतया युक्ता सौभाग्येनोद्यमेन च ।
सम्यगाराध्य भर्तारं तत्रैनं वशमानयेत् ॥ 57
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मणे पर्वणि स्त्रीधर्मवर्णनं
नाम द्वादशोऽध्याय । 12
स्त्रीधर्मवर्णनम्
1.12.m:
Endowed thus with suitability, good fortune, and exertion, / properly honouring her husband, she should bring him under her influence there.
Thus ends the twelfth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Duties of Women', in the Brāhma Parvan of the venerable Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, consisting of fifty-five thousand verses.
Description of the Duties of Women.

1.13.s:
brahmovāca
prathamaṃ pratibudhyeta pravarteta svakarmasu .
paścādbhṛtyajanasyāpi bhuñjīta ca śayīta ca . . 1
1.13.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
प्रथमं प्रतिबुध्येत प्रवर्तेत स्वकर्मसु ।
पश्चाद्भृत्यजनस्यापि भुञ्जीत च शयीत च ॥ 1
1.13.m: Brahmā said: / She should wake up first and attend to her own duties; / she should eat and sleep after the servants have done so.

1.13.s:
bhartrā virahitā strī ca śvaśurābhyāṃ viśeṣataḥ .
dehalīṃ nātivarteta pratīkāre 1 mahatyapi . . 2
1.13.d:
भर्त्रा विरहिता स्त्री च श्वशुराभ्यां विशेषतः ।
देहलीं नातिवर्तेत प्रतीकारे 1 महत्यपि ॥ 2
1.13.m: A woman separated from her husband, and especially from her in-laws, / should not cross the threshold, even when there is great cause to remedy [a situation].

1.13.s:
utthāya prathamaṃ bharturavijñātā na niṣkramet .
kṣapāyāṃ sāvaśeṣāyāṃ rātrau vā vāsarādiṣu . . 3
1.13.d:
उत्थाय प्रथमं भर्तुरविज्ञाता न निष्क्रमेत् ।
क्षपायां सावशेषायां रात्रौ वा वासरादिषु ॥ 3
1.13.m: Rising first, she should not go out unknown to her husband / while the night still remains, or during the night, or at the start of the day.

1.13.s:
tadvāsabhavanasyaiva śanairāhūya kārmikān .
svavyāpāreṣu tānsarvāṃstatratatra niyojayet . . 4
1.13.d:
तद्वासभवनस्यैव शनैराहूय कार्मिकान् ।
स्वव्यापारेषु तान्सर्वांस्तत्रतत्र नियोजयेत् ॥ 4
1.13.m: Calling the workers quietly from that bedchamber itself, / she should direct them all to their respective tasks, here and there.

1.13.s:
vibuddhasya tato bharturnirvartyāvaśyakaṃ vidhim .
gṛhakāryāṇi sarvāṇi vidadhītāpramādataḥ . . 5
1.13.d:
विबुद्धस्य ततो भर्तुर्निर्वर्त्यावश्यकं विधिम् ।
गृहकार्याणि सर्वाणि विदधीताप्रमादतः ॥ 5
1.13.m: Then, having assisted her husband when he has awakened in his obligatory routine, / she should attend to all household duties without negligence.

1.13.s:
muktvāvāsakanepathyaṃ karmayogyaṃ vidhāya ca .
tatkālocitakartavyamanutiṣṭhedyathākramam . . 6
1.13.d:
मुक्त्वावासकनेपथ्यं कर्मयोग्यं विधाय च ।
तत्कालोचितकर्तव्यमनुतिष्ठेद्यथाक्रमम् ॥ 6
1.13.m: Putting aside her nightclothes and putting on attire suited to work, / she should carry out the duties appropriate to that time in regular order.

1.13.s:
mahānasaṃ susammṛṣṭaṃ cullyādivihitārcanam .
sarvopakaraṇopetamasambādhamanāvilam . . 7
1.13.d:
महानसं सुसम्मृष्टं चुल्ल्यादिविहितार्चनम् ।
सर्वोपकरणोपेतमसम्बाधमनाविलम् ॥ 7
1.13.m: The kitchen should be thoroughly swept, the hearth and other [appliances] worshipped, / furnished with all utensils, uncrowded, and clean;

1.13.s:
na cātiguhyaṃ prakaṭaṃ pravibhaktakriyāśrayam .
bharturāptajanākīrṇaṃ gūḍhaṃ kakṣādivarjitam . . 8
1.13.d:
न चातिगुह्यं प्रकटं प्रविभक्तक्रियाश्रयम् ।
भर्तुराप्तजनाकीर्णं गूढं कक्षादिवर्जितम् ॥ 8
1.13.m: neither too secluded nor openly exposed, divided according to activities, / attended by the husband's trusted people, private, and free of alcoves and dark corners.

1.13.s:
tatra pākādibhāṇḍāni bahirantaśca kārayet .
niṇiktamalapaṅkāni śuktivalkādicūrṇakaiḥ . . 9
1.13.d:
तत्र पाकादिभाण्डानि बहिरन्तश्च कारयेत् ।
निणिक्तमलपङ्कानि शुक्तिवल्कादिचूर्णकैः ॥ 9
1.13.m: There she should have the cooking pots and other vessels cleaned inside and out, / their dirt and mire washed away with powders of oyster-shells, bark, and other agents.

1.13.s:
niśi kurvīta dhūmārciḥ śodhitāni divātapaḥ .
dadhipātrāṇi kurvīta sadaivāntaritāni ca . . 1.13.10
1.13.d:
निशि कुर्वीत धूमार्चिः शोधितानि दिवातपः ।
दधिपात्राणि कुर्वीत सदैवान्तरितानि च ॥ 1.13.10
1.13.m: At night she should make them purified with smoke and flame, and by day in the heat of the sun; / and she should always keep the yoghurt pots covered.

1.13.s:
sādhukāritadugdheṣu śodhiteṣu divātape .
īṣadgṛhyoktapātreṣu svacchaṃ yena bhaveddadhi . . 11
1.13.d:
साधुकारितदुग्धेषु शोधितेषु दिवातपे ।
ईषद्गृह्योक्तपात्रेषु स्वच्छं येन भवेद्दधि ॥ 11
1.13.m: In vessels prescribed by the householder, well heated with milk and cleansed in the daytime sun, / so that the yoghurt turns out pure;

1.13.s:
snehagorasapākādi kṛtvā supratyayekṣitam .
kuryātsvayamadhiṣṭhāya bhartuḥ pākavidhikriyām . . 12
1.13.d:
स्नेहगोरसपाकादि कृत्वा सुप्रत्ययेक्षितम् ।
कुर्यात्स्वयमधिष्ठाय भर्तुः पाकविधिक्रियाम् ॥ 12
1.13.m: having cooked fats, dairy, and other foods under reliable supervision, / she herself should preside and conduct the preparation of her husband's food.

1.13.s:
kiṃ priyaṃ ca kimāgneyaṃ ṣaḍrasābhyantareṣu ca .
kiṃ pathyaṃ kimapathyaṃ ca svāsthyaṃ2 vāsya kathaṃ bhavet . .
iti yatnādvijānīyādanuṣṭheyaṃ ca tattathā . . . 13
1.13.d:
किं प्रियं च किमाग्नेयं षड्रसाभ्यन्तरेषु च ।
किं पथ्यं किमपथ्यं च स्वास्थ्यं2 वास्य कथं भवेत् ॥
इति यत्नाद्विजानीयादनुष्ठेयं च तत्तथा ॥ । 13
1.13.m: 'What is liked, what promotes digestive fire among the six tastes, / what is wholesome and what is unwholesome, and how will his health be maintained?' / Thus she should diligently learn, and act accordingly.

1.13.s:
nityānurāgaṃ satkāramāhāraṃ suparīkṣitam .
mahānasādau kurvīta janamāptaṃ kramāgatam . . 14
1.13.d:
नित्यानुरागं सत्कारमाहारं सुपरीक्षितम् ।
महानसादौ कुर्वीत जनमाप्तं क्रमागतम् ॥ 14
1.13.m: In the kitchen and other areas, she should employ trusted people of hereditary service / who show constant devotion, respect, and who thoroughly inspect the food.

1.13.s:
śatru dāyādasambandhaṃ kruddhabhītāvamānitam .
avācyopagṛhītaṃ vā naivamādīni yojayet . . 15
1.13.d:
शत्रु दायादसम्बन्धं क्रुद्धभीतावमानितम् ।
अवाच्योपगृहीतं वा नैवमादीनि योजयेत् ॥ 15
1.13.m: One who is allied with an enemy or an heir, an angry, frightened, or humiliated person, / or one implicated in scandal—such individuals she should never employ.

1.13.s:
punaḥ punaḥ pratiṣṭhāpya guptaṃ svayamadhiṣṭhitam .
bharturāhārapānādi vidadhyādapramādataḥ . . 16
1.13.d:
पुनः पुनः प्रतिष्ठाप्य गुप्तं स्वयमधिष्ठितम् ।
भर्तुराहारपानादि विदध्यादप्रमादतः ॥ 16
1.13.m: Again and again setting it down, guarded and supervised in person, / she should prepare her husband's food and drink without negligence.

1.13.s:
pākaṃ nirvartya mātrāṇāṃ kṛtvā svedapramārjanam .
gandhatāmbūlamālyādi kiñcidādāya mātrayā . . 17
1.13.d:
पाकं निर्वर्त्य मात्राणां कृत्वा स्वेदप्रमार्जनम् ।
गन्धताम्बूलमाल्यादि किञ्चिदादाय मात्रया ॥ 17
1.13.m: Having completed the cooking of the dishes and wiped away her sweat, / taking a little fragrance, betel, garlands, and other items in moderation,

1.13.s:
yathaucityāditatkāle bharturvinayasambhramaiḥ .
tatkālānugatātyarthamāhāramupapādayet . . 18
1.13.d:
यथौचित्यादितत्काले भर्तुर्विनयसम्भ्रमैः ।
तत्कालानुगतात्यर्थमाहारमुपपादयेत् ॥ 18
1.13.m: at the proper time according to propriety, with deference and respect toward her husband, / she should serve the meal, closely adapted to that time.

1.13.s:
svabhāvāmayakālānāṃ vaiparītyena sarvadā .
sarvamāhārapānādi prayojyaṃ tadvido jaguḥ . . 19
1.13.d:
स्वभावामयकालानां वैपरीत्येन सर्वदा ।
सर्वमाहारपानादि प्रयोज्यं तद्विदो जगुः ॥ 19
1.13.m: All food and drink should always be served / contrary to [the aggravate nature of] constitution, disease, and season, so say those who know.

1.13.s:
hīnatulyādhikatvena bhartā paśyati yaṃ yathā .
taṃ tathaivādhikaṃ paśyennyāyataḥ pratipattiṣu . . 1.13.20
1.13.d:
हीनतुल्याधिकत्वेन भर्ता पश्यति यं यथा ।
तं तथैवाधिकं पश्येन्न्यायतः प्रतिपत्तिषु ॥ 1.13.20
1.13.m: Whomever the husband regards as inferior, equal, or superior, / she should regard that very person as even higher, in accordance with justice and courtesies.

1.13.s:
sāpatnakānyapatyāni paśyetsvebhyo viśeṣataḥ .
bhaginīvatsapatnīśca tadvadhūnnijabandhuvat . . 21
1.13.d:
सापत्नकान्यपत्यानि पश्येत्स्वेभ्यो विशेषतः ।
भगिनीवत्सपत्नीश्च तद्वधून्निजबन्धुवत् ॥ 21
1.13.m: She should look upon the children of cowives even more favourably than her own, / and upon cowives as sisters, and their daughters-in-law as her own kin.

1.13.s:
grāsācchādaśirobhyaṅgasnānamaṇḍanakādikam .
sapatnīnāmakṛtvā tu ātmano'pi na kārayet . . 22
1.13.d:
ग्रासाच्छादशिरोभ्यङ्गस्नानमण्डनकादिकम् ।
सपत्नीनामकृत्वा तु आत्मनोऽपि न कारयेत् ॥ 22
1.13.m: Food, clothing, oiling of the head, bathing, ornamentation, and the like / she should not have done for herself without first providing them to her cowives.

1.13.s:
vyādhitānāṃ cikitsārthamauṣadhādikamādarāt .
vidadhyādātmanastāsāṃ sarvāśritajanasya ca . . 23
1.13.d:
व्याधितानां चिकित्सार्थमौषधादिकमादरात् ।
विदध्यादात्मनस्तासां सर्वाश्रितजनस्य च ॥ 23
1.13.m: For treating the sick, she should attentively provide / medicines and other needs for herself, for them, and for all dependants.

1.13.s:
tacchoke śucamādadyāttattuṣṭau mudamāvahet .
bhṛtyabandhusapatnīnāṃ tulyaduḥkhasukhā bhavet . . 24
1.13.d:
तच्छोके शुचमादद्यात्तत्तुष्टौ मुदमावहेत् ।
भृत्यबन्धुसपत्नीनां तुल्यदुःखसुखा भवेत् ॥ 24
1.13.m: She should grieve at their sorrow and rejoice at their joy; / she should share equally the pleasure and pain of servants, relatives, and cowives.

1.13.s:
lagdhāvakāśā svapyācya niśi suptotthitā kramāt .
anyatra vyayakartāraṃ patiṃ rahasi bodhayet . . 25
1.13.d:
लग्धावकाशा स्वप्याच्य निशि सुप्तोत्थिता क्रमात् ।
अन्यत्र व्ययकर्तारं पतिं रहसि बोधयेत् ॥ 25
1.13.m: Having found an opportunity after lying down, rising in due course during the night, / she should privately advise her husband if he spends money elsewhere.

1.13.s:
yadavadyaṃ sapatnīnāṃ svayamasmai na tadvadet .
dauḥśīlyādi tu sāpāyaṃ gūḍhamasmai nivedayet . . 26
durbhagāmanapatyāṃ vā bhartrā cātitiraskṛtām . 1
1.13.d:
यदवद्यं सपत्नीनां स्वयमस्मै न तद्वदेत् ।
दौःशील्यादि तु सापायं गूढमस्मै निवेदयेत् ॥ 26
दुर्भगामनपत्यां वा भर्त्रा चातितिरस्कृताम् । 1
1.13.m:
She should not herself speak to him of what is blameworthy in her cowives; / but she should secretly report to him bad conduct and the like which causes harm.
A cowife who is unfortunate, childless, or greatly disfavoured by her husband—

1.13.s: aduṣṭāṃ samyamāśvāsya tenaitāmanukūlayet . . 27
1.13.d: अदुष्टां सम्यमाश्वास्य तेनैतामनुकूलयेत् ॥ 27
1.13.m: if she is free of malice, [the wife] should console her with restraint and make him favourable toward her.

1.13.s:
tathā vāgdaṇḍapāruṣyairjanaṃ bhartrā vipīḍitam .
kuryādvidheyamāśvāsya na ceddoṣāya tadbhavet . . 28
1.13.d:
तथा वाग्दण्डपारुष्यैर्जनं भर्त्रा विपीडितम् ।
कुर्याद्विधेयमाश्वास्य न चेद्दोषाय तद्भवेत् ॥ 28
1.13.m: Likewise, she should comfort a person tormented by her husband through harsh words or punishment / and make that person obedient, if doing so does not lead to harm.

1.13.s:
matvātmanonapatyatvaṃ kālaṃ cāpi gataṃ bahum .
santānādikamuddiśya kāryamātmanivedanam . . 29
1.13.d:
मत्वात्मनोनपत्यत्वं कालं चापि गतं बहुम् ।
सन्तानादिकमुद्दिश्य कार्यमात्मनिवेदनम् ॥ 29
1.13.m: Reflecting on her own childlessness and that much time has passed, / she should make an offering of herself for the sake of offspring and lineage.

1.13.s:
yaccānyadapi jānīyātkiñcidasya cikīrṣitam .
tatkilājānatīvāsya siddhameva pradarśayet . . 1.13.30
1.13.d:
यच्चान्यदपि जानीयात्किञ्चिदस्य चिकीर्षितम् ।
तत्किलाजानतीवास्य सिद्धमेव प्रदर्शयेत् ॥ 1.13.30
1.13.m: Whatever else she knows he desires to do, / she should present it as already accomplished, as if without his even knowing.

1.13.s:
vaivāhikaṃ vidhiṃ bhartuḥ sarvaṃ kṛtvā sasambhramam .
pariṇītā ca tāṃ paśyennityaṃ bhaginikāmiva . . 31
1.13.d:
वैवाहिकं विधिं भर्तुः सर्वं कृत्वा ससम्भ्रमम् ।
परिणीता च तां पश्येन्नित्यं भगिनिकामिव ॥ 31
1.13.m: Having performed all the marriage rites for her husband with eager care, / she should continually look upon the newly wedded bride as a younger sister.

1.13.s:
pūjāṃ sambandhivargasya maṅgalaṃ maṅgalāni ca .
kuryādabhinavoḍhāyāḥ suprahaṣṭena cetasā . . 32
1.13.d:
पूजां सम्बन्धिवर्गस्य मङ्गलं मङ्गलानि च ।
कुर्यादभिनवोढायाः सुप्रहष्टेन चेतसा ॥ 32
1.13.m: With an exceedingly joyful heart, she should honour the circle of relatives / and perform auspicious rites for the new bride.

1.13.s:
mātṛvacchikṣayedenāṃ gṛhakṛtyeṣvamatsarā .
pradeśikavidhiṃ vāsyā vidadhyādyatnataḥ svayam . . 33
1.13.d:
मातृवच्छिक्षयेदेनां गृहकृत्येष्वमत्सरा ।
प्रदेशिकविधिं वास्या विदध्याद्यत्नतः स्वयम् ॥ 33
1.13.m: Free from jealousy, she should instruct her like a mother in household duties, / or personally arrange regional customs for her with care.

1.13.s:
evaṃ bharturabhiprāya sarvamityādikārayet .
sukhārthaṃ vāpi santyajya strīṇāṃ bhartādhidevatā . . 34
1.13.d:
एवं भर्तुरभिप्राय सर्वमित्यादिकारयेत् ।
सुखार्थं वापि सन्त्यज्य स्त्रीणां भर्ताधिदेवता ॥ 34
1.13.m: In this way she should fulfill every desire of her husband and the rest; / or, setting aside her own pleasure, [remember that] the husband is the supreme deity for women.

1.13.s:
bhartādhidevatā nāryā varṇā brāhmadevatāḥ .
brāhmaṇā hyagnidevāstu prajā rājanyadevatāḥ . . 35
1.13.d:
भर्ताधिदेवता नार्या वर्णा ब्राह्मदेवताः ।
ब्राह्मणा ह्यग्निदेवास्तु प्रजा राजन्यदेवताः ॥ 35
1.13.m: The husband is the supreme deity of a woman; Brahmā is the deity of the castes; / the brāhmaṇas have Agni as their deity; subjects have the king as their deity.

1.13.s:
tāsāṃ trivargasaṃsiddhau pradiṣṭaṃ kāraṇadvayam .
bharturyadanukūlatvaṃ yacca śīlamaviplutam . . 36
1.13.d:
तासां त्रिवर्गसंसिद्धौ प्रदिष्टं कारणद्वयम् ।
भर्तुर्यदनुकूलत्वं यच्च शीलमविप्लुतम् ॥ 36
1.13.m: Two causes are taught for their attainment of the three aims of life: / being agreeable to the husband, and unfailing good character.

1.13.s:
na tathā yauvanaṃ loke nāpi rūpaṃ na bhūṣaṇam .
yathā priyānukūlatvaṃ siddhaṃ śaśvadanauṣadham . . 37
1.13.d:
न तथा यौवनं लोके नापि रूपं न भूषणम् ।
यथा प्रियानुकूलत्वं सिद्धं शश्वदनौषधम् ॥ 37
1.13.m: Neither youth, nor beauty, nor ornaments in this world / succeed like being agreeable to one's beloved, which is an ever-effective charm.

1.13.s:
vayorūpādihāriṇyo dṛśyante durbhagāḥ striyaḥ .
vallabhā mandarūpāśca bahvyo galitayauvanāḥ . . 38
1.13.d:
वयोरूपादिहारिण्यो दृश्यन्ते दुर्भगाः स्त्रियः ।
वल्लभा मन्दरूपाश्च बह्व्यो गलितयौवनाः ॥ 38
1.13.m: Women captivating in age, beauty, and the like are seen to be unfortunate, / while many of modest beauty and faded youth are beloved.

1.13.s:
tasmātpriyatvaṃ lokānāṃ nidānaṃ 1yogyatāparam .
tāṃ vinānye guṇā vandhyāḥ sarve'narthakṛto'pi vā . . 39
1.13.d:
तस्मात्प्रियत्वं लोकानां निदानं 1योग्यतापरम् ।
तां विनान्ये गुणा वन्ध्याः सर्वेऽनर्थकृतोऽपि वा ॥ 39
1.13.m: Therefore, being dear to people has fitness as its primary cause; / without that, all other virtues are barren or even cause misfortune.

1.13.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena vidadhyādātmayogyatām .
paracittajñatā cāsyā mūlaṃ sarvakriyāsviha . .1.13.4 0
bahirāgacchato jñātvā kālaṃ saṃmṛjya bhūmikām .
sajjīkṛtāsanā tiṣṭhettasyājñāṃ pratitatparā . . 41
1.13.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन विदध्यादात्मयोग्यताम् ।
परचित्तज्ञता चास्या मूलं सर्वक्रियास्विह ॥1.13.4 0
बहिरागच्छतो ज्ञात्वा कालं संमृज्य भूमिकाम् ।
सज्जीकृतासना तिष्ठेत्तस्याज्ञां प्रतितत्परा ॥ 41
1.13.m: Therefore, with every effort she should cultivate her own fitness; / and knowing the minds of others is the root of this in all actions here. / Knowing the time of his return from outside, sweeping the floor, / she should remain with a seat prepared, intent on his command.

1.13.s:
svayaṃ prakṣālayetpādāvutthāpya paricārikām .
tālavṛntādikaiḥ kuryācchamasvedāpanodanam . . 42
1.13.d:
स्वयं प्रक्षालयेत्पादावुत्थाप्य परिचारिकाम् ।
तालवृन्तादिकैः कुर्याच्छमस्वेदापनोदनम् ॥ 42
1.13.m: She should wash his feet herself, having made the maidservant stand aside; / with a palm-leaf fan and the like she should remove his fatigue and sweat.

1.13.s:
āhārasnānapānādau saspṛhaṃ yatra lakṣayet .
tadiṃgitajñā tattvena siddhamasmai nivedayet . . 43
1.13.d:
आहारस्नानपानादौ सस्पृहं यत्र लक्षयेत् ।
तदिंगितज्ञा तत्त्वेन सिद्धमस्मै निवेदयेत् ॥ 43
1.13.m: Wherever she notices his desire for food, bathing, drink, and the like, / discerning his gestures, she should truthfully present to him what is prepared.

1.13.s:
sapantīpatibandhūnāṃ bhartṛcittānukūlyataḥ .
pratipattiṃ prayuñjīta svabandhūnāṃ na vai tathā . . 44
1.13.d:
सपन्तीपतिबन्धूनां भर्तृचित्तानुकूल्यतः ।
प्रतिपत्तिं प्रयुञ्जीत स्वबन्धूनां न वै तथा ॥ 44
1.13.m: By conforming to her husband's mind she should show respect / to the relatives of co-wives and of her husband, but not in that way to her own relatives.

1.13.s:
teṣu cātmani ca jñātvā bhartṛcittaṃ prasādayet .
pratipattiṃ tathāpyeṣāṃ nādriyeta svabandhuṣu . . 45
1.13.d:
तेषु चात्मनि च ज्ञात्वा भर्तृचित्तं प्रसादयेत् ।
प्रतिपत्तिं तथाप्येषां नाद्रियेत स्वबन्धुषु ॥ 45
1.13.m: Understanding the husband's mind toward them and toward herself, she should please him; / nevertheless, she should not pay such respect to her own relatives.

1.13.s:
api bharturabhipretaṃ nārī tatkulavāsinī .
satkārairnijabandhūnāṃ tena nopaiti vācyatām . .46
1.13.d:
अपि भर्तुरभिप्रेतं नारी तत्कुलवासिनी ।
सत्कारैर्निजबन्धूनां तेन नोपैति वाच्यताम् ॥46
1.13.m: Even if desired by the husband, a woman living in his family / does not incur reproach by treating her own relatives with hospitality.

1.13.s:
pūjya eva hi sambandhaḥ sarvāvasthāsu yoṣitām .
kastato'pyupakārāṃśaṃ lipseta kulajaḥ pumān . .47
1.13.d:
पूज्य एव हि सम्बन्धः सर्वावस्थासु योषिताम् ।
कस्ततोऽप्युपकारांशं लिप्सेत कुलजः पुमान् ॥47
1.13.m: For an alliance with women is indeed venerable in all circumstances; / what well-born man would seek even a portion of benefit from it?

1.13.s:
sampūjya svasutāṃ tasmai vidhivatpratipādyate .
tato'syā lipsate nāma kimakāryamataḥ param . . 48
1.13.d:
सम्पूज्य स्वसुतां तस्मै विधिवत्प्रतिपाद्यते ।
ततोऽस्या लिप्सते नाम किमकार्यमतः परम् ॥ 48
1.13.m: Having honoured [the groom], one's daughter is given to him according to rule; / if one seeks [gain] from her, what greater misdeed could there be than this?

1.13.s:
kanyāṃ pradāya yairvṛttirātmanaḥ parikalpyate .
dāsabhaṇḍanaṭādīnāṃ mārgo'yaṃ na mahātmanām . .49
1.13.d:
कन्यां प्रदाय यैर्वृत्तिरात्मनः परिकल्प्यते ।
दासभण्डनटादीनां मार्गोऽयं न महात्मनाम् ॥49
1.13.m: Those who devise their own livelihood by giving away a daughter— / this is the path of slaves, buffoons, dancers, and the like, not of noble souls.

1.13.s:
tasmātstrībāṃdhavā nityaṃ prītimātraikasādhinīm .
pratipattiṃ samādadyuḥ sambandhibhyaḥ prasaṃginīm . 1.13.50
1.13.d:
तस्मात्स्त्रीबांधवा नित्यं प्रीतिमात्रैकसाधिनीम् ।
प्रतिपत्तिं समादद्युः सम्बन्धिभ्यः प्रसंगिनीम् । 1.13.50
