1.13.m: Therefore, the relatives of a woman should always accept from relations by marriage / only such ongoing respect as produces affection alone.

1.13.s:
tasyā bhartari rakṣeta prītiṃ loke ca vācyatām .
ātmano'satpravādaṃ ca ceṣṭeransādhuvṛttayaḥ . . 51
1.13.d:
तस्या भर्तरि रक्षेत प्रीतिं लोके च वाच्यताम् ।
आत्मनोऽसत्प्रवादं च चेष्टेरन्साधुवृत्तयः ॥ 51
1.13.m: They should protect her affection toward her husband and her [good] name in the world; / those of virtuous conduct should guard against ill report of themselves.

1.13.s:
evaṃ vijñāya sadvṛttaṃ strī varteta tathā sadā .
yena tatparivargasya bhavedbhartuśca sammatā . . 52
1.13.d:
एवं विज्ञाय सद्वृत्तं स्त्री वर्तेत तथा सदा ।
येन तत्परिवर्गस्य भवेद्भर्तुश्च सम्मता ॥ 52
1.13.m: Knowing virtuous conduct thus, a woman should always conduct herself / in such a way that she is approved by his family and by her husband.

1.13.s:
priyāpi sādhuvṛttāpi vikhyātābhijanāpi ca .
janāpavādātsamprāpa sītānarthaṃ sudāruṇam . . 53
1.13.d:
प्रियापि साधुवृत्तापि विख्याताभिजनापि च ।
जनापवादात्सम्प्राप सीतानर्थं सुदारुणम् ॥ 53
1.13.m: Even though beloved, of virtuous conduct, and of celebrated lineage, / Sītā suffered terrible misfortune because of public slander.

1.13.s:
sarvasyāmiṣabhūtatvādguṇadoṣānabhijñataḥ .
prāyeṇāvinayaucityātstrīṇāṃ vṛttaṃ hi duṣkaram . . 54
1.13.d:
सर्वस्यामिषभूतत्वाद्गुणदोषानभिज्ञतः ।
प्रायेणाविनयौचित्यात्स्त्रीणां वृत्तं हि दुष्करम् ॥ 54
1.13.m: Because everything becomes prey, from ignorance of virtues and faults, / and generally from the prevalence of indiscretion, conduct is difficult for women.

1.13.s:
agṛhyatvānmanovṛtteḥ prāyaḥ kapaṭadarśanāt .
niraṅkuśatvāllokasya nirvācyā viralāḥ striyaḥ . . 55
1.13.d:
अगृह्यत्वान्मनोवृत्तेः प्रायः कपटदर्शनात् ।
निरङ्कुशत्वाल्लोकस्य निर्वाच्या विरलाः स्त्रियः ॥ 55
1.13.m: Because the mind's workings cannot be grasped, because deceit is often seen, / and because the world is unrestrained, women free from reproach are rare.

1.13.s:
daivayogādayogatvādvyavahārānabhijñataḥ .
vācyatāpattayo dṛṣṭāḥ strīṇāṃ śuddhe'pi cetasi . . 56
1.13.d:
दैवयोगादयोगत्वाद्व्यवहारानभिज्ञतः ।
वाच्यतापत्तयो दृष्टाः स्त्रीणां शुद्धेऽपि चेतसि ॥ 56
1.13.m: Through fate, through impropriety, and through ignorance of worldly dealings, / falls into reproach are seen for women even when their heart is pure.

1.13.s:
tāsāṃ daivapratīkāro nopabhogādṛte bhavet .
cāritraṃ lokavṛttaṃ ca etayorvidurauṣadham . . 57
1.13.d:
तासां दैवप्रतीकारो नोपभोगादृते भवेत् ।
चारित्रं लोकवृत्तं च एतयोर्विदुरौषधम् ॥ 57
1.13.m: For them there is no remedy against fate without experiencing it; / good character and worldly wisdom are known as the remedy for the other two.

1.13.s:
hiṃdolakādikrīḍāyāṃ prasaktāṃ taruṇīṃ niśi .
ramamāṇāṃ viṭaiḥ sārdhaṃ vidhavāṃ svairacāriṇīm . . 58
1.13.d:
हिंदोलकादिक्रीडायां प्रसक्तां तरुणीं निशि ।
रममाणां विटैः सार्धं विधवां स्वैरचारिणीम् ॥ 58
1.13.m: A young woman devoted to playing on a swing and the like at night, / a widow wandering at will and sporting with rakes,

1.13.s:
vṛddhādibhāryāṃ 1sajjāyāṃ yānageyādisaṃginīm .
kaḥ śraddadhyātsatītyevaṃ sādhvīmapi hi yoṣitam . . 59
1.13.d:
वृद्धादिभार्यां 1सज्जायां यानगेयादिसंगिनीम् ।
कः श्रद्दध्यात्सतीत्येवं साध्वीमपि हि योषितम् ॥ 59
1.13.m: the wife of an old man or the like, dressed up and taking part in processions, singing, and such— / who would believe even a virtuous woman to be chaste in these cases?

1.13.s:
yau cāsāmiṅgitākārau sandigdhārthaprasādhakau .
tayostattvaparijñānaṃ viṣayo yogināṃ2 yadi . . 1.13.60
1.13.d:
यौ चासामिङ्गिताकारौ सन्दिग्धार्थप्रसाधकौ ।
तयोस्तत्त्वपरिज्ञानं विषयो योगिनां2 यदि ॥ 1.13.60
1.13.m: And as for the gesture and facial expression of these [women], which determine doubtful matters, / true understanding of both is a domain for yogins, if at all.

1.13.s:
tasmādyathoktamācāramanutiṣṭhetsusaṃyatā .
mithyālagnopyasadvādaḥ kampayatyeva tatkulam . . 61
1.13.d:
तस्माद्यथोक्तमाचारमनुतिष्ठेत्सुसंयता ।
मिथ्यालग्नोप्यसद्वादः कम्पयत्येव तत्कुलम् ॥ 61
1.13.m: Therefore, properly restrained, she should perform customary conduct as taught; / false gossip, even when falsely attached, shakes the entire family.

1.13.s:
trikulyā vācyatā rakṣyā pratiṣṭhāpyatha santatiḥ .
bhartustrivargasiddhiśca sādhyaṃ tatkulayoṣitām . . 62
1.13.d:
त्रिकुल्या वाच्यता रक्ष्या प्रतिष्ठाप्यथ सन्ततिः ।
भर्तुस्त्रिवर्गसिद्धिश्च साध्यं तत्कुलयोषिताम् ॥ 62
1.13.m: Reproach of the three families must be prevented, offspring established, / and the husband's accomplishment of the three aims of life achieved by women of that family.

1.13.s:
pātayantyeva dauḥśīlyādātmānaṃ sakulatrayam .
uddharanti tadaivaitāḥ striyaścāritrabhūṣaṇāḥ . . 63
1.13.d:
पातयन्त्येव दौःशील्यादात्मानं सकुलत्रयम् ।
उद्धरन्ति तदैवैताः स्त्रियश्चारित्रभूषणाः ॥ 63
1.13.m: Through bad character they bring down themselves and their three families; / but adorned with good conduct, women elevate them at once.

1.13.s:
bhartṛcittānukūlatvaṃ yāsāṃ śīlamavicyutam3 .
tāsāṃ ratnasuvarṇādi bhāra eva na maṇḍanam . . 64
1.13.d:
भर्तृचित्तानुकूलत्वं यासां शीलमविच्युतम्3 ।
तासां रत्नसुवर्णादि भार एव न मण्डनम् ॥ 64
1.13.m: For those whose conduct is conforming to their husband's mind and whose virtue is unswerving, / jewels, gold, and the like are merely a burden, not an ornament.

1.13.s:
lokajñāne parā koṭiḥ patyau bhaktiśca śāśvatī .
śuddhānvayānāṃ nārīṇāṃ vidyādetatkulavratam . . 65
1.13.d:
लोकज्ञाने परा कोटिः पत्यौ भक्तिश्च शाश्वती ।
शुद्धान्वयानां नारीणां विद्यादेतत्कुलव्रतम् ॥ 65
1.13.m: The highest degree of worldly knowledge and constant devotion to her husband: / one should know this as the family vow of women of pure lineage.

1.13.s:
tasmāllokaśca bhartā ca samyagārādhito yayā .
dharmamarthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca saivāpnoti niratyayā . . 66
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi strīdharmakathanaṃ
nāma trayodaśo'dhyāyaḥ . 13 .
patiparadeśavāse strīṇāṃ śṛṅgāraniṣedhaḥ
1.13.d:
तस्माल्लोकश्च भर्ता च सम्यगाराधितो यया ।
धर्ममर्थं च कामं च सैवाप्नोति निरत्यया ॥ 66
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि स्त्रीधर्मकथनं
नाम त्रयोदशोऽध्यायः । 13 ।
पतिपरदेशवासे स्त्रीणां शृङ्गारनिषेधः
1.13.m:
Therefore, she by whom the world and her husband are properly honoured / attains dharma, wealth, and pleasure without impediment.
Thus, in the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the fifty-thousand-verse compendium, in the Brāhmaparvan, the thirteenth chapter, called 'Explanation of the Duties of Women.'
Prohibition of ornamentation for women when the husband is residing abroad.

1.14.s:
brahmovāca
preṣite maṇḍanaṃ strīṇāṃ patyau maṅgalamātrakam .
niṣpādanaṃ ca yatnena tadārabdhasya karmaṇaḥ . . 1
1.14.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
प्रेषिते मण्डनं स्त्रीणां पत्यौ मङ्गलमात्रकम् ।
निष्पादनं च यत्नेन तदारब्धस्य कर्मणः ॥ 1
1.14.m: Brahmā said: / When her husband has gone abroad, women's ornament should be merely what is auspicious, / and the diligent execution of the work begun by him;

1.14.s: śayyāmupārjanamarthānāṃ vyayānāṃ parihāpaṇam . . 2
1.14.d: शय्यामुपार्जनमर्थानां व्ययानां परिहापणम् ॥ 2
1.14.m: [keeping to her] bed, the acquisition of wealth, and the curtailment of expenses;

1.14.s:
vratopavāsatātparyaṃ tadvārtāparimārgaṇam .
daivajñekṣaṇikapraśno devānāmupayācanam . . 3
1.14.d:
व्रतोपवासतात्पर्यं तद्वार्तापरिमार्गणम् ।
दैवज्ञेक्षणिकप्रश्नो देवानामुपयाचनम् ॥ 3
1.14.m: devotion to vows and fasts, inquiring after news of him, / questioning astrologers and diviners, and making vows to the gods;

1.14.s:
nityaṃ tasyāgamāśaṃsā kṣemārthaṃ devapūjanam .
na cātyujjvalaveṣatvaṃ na sadā tailadhāraṇam . .4
1.14.d:
नित्यं तस्यागमाशंसा क्षेमार्थं देवपूजनम् ।
न चात्युज्ज्वलवेषत्वं न सदा तैलधारणम् ॥4
1.14.m: constantly longing for his return, worship of the gods for his welfare, / no excessively bright garments, and not always wearing oil [in her hair].

1.14.s:
jñātiveśma na gantavyaṃ sakāmagamanena 1 ca .
gurūṇāmājñayā yāvadbharturāptajanaiḥ saha . . 5
1.14.d:
ज्ञातिवेश्म न गन्तव्यं सकामगमनेन 1 च ।
गुरूणामाज्ञया यावद्भर्तुराप्तजनैः सह ॥ 5
1.14.m: She should not go to the house of her kinsmen at her own pleasure, / but only by the permission of her elders, together with trustworthy people of her husband.

1.14.s:
tatrāpi na ciraṃ tiṣṭhetsnānādīnvāpi nācaret .
yāvadarthaṃ kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā tataḥ śīghraṃ samācaret . . 6
1.14.d:
तत्रापि न चिरं तिष्ठेत्स्नानादीन्वापि नाचरेत् ।
यावदर्थं क्षणं स्थित्वा ततः शीघ्रं समाचरेत् ॥ 6
1.14.m: Even there she should not stay long, nor perform bathing and the like; / having stayed for a moment as needed, she should then leave quickly.

1.14.s:
āgate prakṛtisthaiva kṛtvā tātkālikaṃ vidhim .
muktapravāsane pathye snāte bhuktavati priye . . 7
1.14.d:
आगते प्रकृतिस्थैव कृत्वा तात्कालिकं विधिम् ।
मुक्तप्रवासने पथ्ये स्नाते भुक्तवति प्रिये ॥ 7
1.14.m: When he has returned, she should remain in her natural state, perform the rites for that time, / and when the beloved has laid aside his travel garments, bathed, and eaten wholesome food,

1.14.s:
ātmānaṃ samalaṅkṛtya saviśeṣaṃ mudānvitā .
devapūjopahārādīndadyātprāgupapāditān . . 8
1.14.d:
आत्मानं समलङ्कृत्य सविशेषं मुदान्विता ।
देवपूजोपहारादीन्दद्यात्प्रागुपपादितान् ॥ 8
1.14.m: having adorned herself exceptionally, filled with joy, / she should present the offerings for the worship of the gods and other things prepared beforehand.

1.14.s:
kaniṣṭhāmātṛvajjyeṣṭhāṃ tadapatyāni cātmavat .
paśyettatparivargaṃ tu nityaṃ svaparivargavat . . 9
1.14.d:
कनिष्ठामातृवज्ज्येष्ठां तदपत्यानि चात्मवत् ।
पश्येत्तत्परिवर्गं तु नित्यं स्वपरिवर्गवत् ॥ 9
1.14.m: She should view the elder [co-wife] like a mother, the younger and her children like herself, / and his retinue always like her own retinue.

1.14.s:
tatpuronāsane tiṣṭhetpatiṃ nāmaṃtrayeta ca .
tadabhiprāyataḥ kuryātpravṛttiṃ sarvakarmasu . . 1.14.10
1.14.d:
तत्पुरोनासने तिष्ठेत्पतिं नामंत्रयेत च ।
तदभिप्रायतः कुर्यात्प्रवृत्तिं सर्वकर्मसु ॥ 1.14.10
1.14.m: She should not sit on a seat before him, nor address her husband by name; / she should engage in all deeds according to his intention.

1.14.s:
na saṃsṛjeta taddviṣṭaiḥ sakhyaṃ kurvīta tatpriyaiḥ .
janamāptatamaṃ tasya sadābhartuśca mānayet . . 11
1.14.d:
न संसृजेत तद्द्विष्टैः सख्यं कुर्वीत तत्प्रियैः ।
जनमाप्ततमं तस्य सदाभर्तुश्च मानयेत् ॥ 11
1.14.m: She should not associate with those he dislikes; she should make friends with those he loves; / and she should always honour the person who is most trusted by her husband.

1.14.s:
paitṛkātsamupānītaṃ vasusaugaṃdhikādikam .
tasmai nivedyātmatayā tadā tadupayojayet . . 12
1.14.d:
पैतृकात्समुपानीतं वसुसौगंधिकादिकम् ।
तस्मै निवेद्यात्मतया तदा तदुपयोजयेत् ॥ 12
1.14.m: Wealth, perfumes, and the like brought from her father's family / she should use only after offering them to him as his own.

1.14.s:
sopi tatprītaye kiṃcidādadyādalpamūlyakam .
saṃgopya mātṛvatstheyaṃ tattathaivopayojayet . . 13
1.14.d:
सोपि तत्प्रीतये किंचिदादद्यादल्पमूल्यकम् ।
संगोप्य मातृवत्स्थेयं तत्तथैवोपयोजयेत् ॥ 13
1.14.m: He too may accept something of small value to please her; / keeping it secret like a mother, she should use it just as it is.

1.14.s:
tatprītyarthaṃ gṛhītaṃ yadvailakṣyādinivṛttaye .
saviśeṣaṃ prasaṃgena tasyaitatpratipādayet 1 . . 14
1.14.d:
तत्प्रीत्यर्थं गृहीतं यद्वैलक्ष्यादिनिवृत्तये ।
सविशेषं प्रसंगेन तस्यैतत्प्रतिपादयेत् 1 ॥ 14
1.14.m: Whatever is accepted to please her, in order to dispel embarrassment and the like, / she should present to him especially when the occasion arises.

1.14.s:
strīṇāṃ yadetatsāpatnyaṃ paraṃ mātsaryakāraṇam .
tasmāttatparihartavyaṃ paramodāracaryayā2 . . 15
1.14.d:
स्त्रीणां यदेतत्सापत्न्यं परं मात्सर्यकारणम् ।
तस्मात्तत्परिहर्तव्यं परमोदारचर्यया2 ॥ 15
1.14.m: This rivalry of co-wives is the supreme cause of jealousy for women; / therefore, it should be avoided by supremely noble conduct.

1.14.s:
tathā kalpitanepathyā bhartuḥ paryāyavāsare .
hriyamādayamāneva3 patiṃ gacchedvisarjitā . . 16
1.14.d:
तथा कल्पितनेपथ्या भर्तुः पर्यायवासरे ।
ह्रियमादयमानेव3 पतिं गच्छेद्विसर्जिता ॥ 16
1.14.m: Likewise, adorned with attire arranged on her husband's allotted night, / she should go to her husband when dismissed [by the senior wife], acting as if struck by modesty.

1.14.s:
gatvā rahasi bhartāraṃ tatkālocitasaṃbhramaiḥ .
tadbhāvānugataistaistaiḥ saviśeṣamupācaret . . 17
1.14.d:
गत्वा रहसि भर्तारं तत्कालोचितसंभ्रमैः ।
तद्भावानुगतैस्तैस्तैः सविशेषमुपाचरेत् ॥ 17
1.14.m: Having approached her husband in secret, she should attend upon him with special care, / through various agitations suitable to the occasion and conforming to his moods.

1.14.s:
pratibudhya tataḥ kāle saviśeṣaṃ trapānvitā .
jyeṣṭhāya vasatiṃ gacchedviśeṣeṇa tathā punaḥ . . 18
1.14.d:
प्रतिबुध्य ततः काले सविशेषं त्रपान्विता ।
ज्येष्ठाय वसतिं गच्छेद्विशेषेण तथा पुनः ॥ 18
1.14.m: Having awakened in the morning at the proper time, exceptionally filled with shame, / she should again go specifically to the dwelling of the senior wife.

1.14.s:
aprātikūlyaṃ jyeṣṭhāyā hitamanyatra yoṣitaḥ .
tataḥ śanaistvavacchidya patiṃ svavaśamānayet . . 19
1.14.d:
अप्रातिकूल्यं ज्येष्ठाया हितमन्यत्र योषितः ।
ततः शनैस्त्ववच्छिद्य पतिं स्ववशमानयेत् ॥ 19
1.14.m: Benevolence toward the senior wife, and never antagonism, is beneficial elsewhere for a woman; / then, having detached her husband gradually, she should bring him under her own sway.

1.14.s:
bahiṣpākādiyogena catuḥṣaṣṭyā rahogatam .
jyeṣṭhāmatiśayāneva bhartāramuparañjayet . . 1.14.20
1.14.d:
बहिष्पाकादियोगेन चतुःषष्ट्या रहोगतम् ।
ज्येष्ठामतिशयानेव भर्तारमुपरञ्जयेत् ॥ 1.14.20
1.14.m: Through cooking outside and the like, and through the sixty-four arts when alone, / outdoing the senior wife, she should delight her husband.

1.14.s:
prāgalbhyaṃ rahasi strīṇāṃ lajjādhikyaṃ tato'nyadā .
cittajñānānuvṛttiśca patyau saṃsevanaṃ param . . 21
1.14.d:
प्रागल्भ्यं रहसि स्त्रीणां लज्जाधिक्यं ततोऽन्यदा ।
चित्तज्ञानानुवृत्तिश्च पत्यौ संसेवनं परम् ॥ 21
1.14.m: Boldness in secret for women, but greater bashfulness at other times, / and following the knowledge of his mind—this is supreme service to the husband.

1.14.s:
evamārādhya bhartāraṃ gṛhamākramya ca kramāt .
gauravaṃ pratipattiṃ vā jyeṣṭhādiṣu na hāpayet . . 22
1.14.d:
एवमाराध्य भर्तारं गृहमाक्रम्य च क्रमात् ।
गौरवं प्रतिपत्तिं वा ज्येष्ठादिषु न हापयेत् ॥ 22
1.14.m: Having thus gratified her husband and gradually taken over the household, / she should not diminish reverence or honor toward the senior wife and others.

1.14.s:
gṛhavyāpāradāneṣu patiṃ guḍhaṃ tadhā vadet .
adhikuryādanicchantī jyeṣṭhaivenāṃ yathā balāt . . 23
1.14.d:
गृहव्यापारदानेषु पतिं गुढं तधा वदेत् ।
अधिकुर्यादनिच्छन्ती ज्येष्ठैवेनां यथा बलात् ॥ 23
1.14.m: In assigning household duties, she should speak secretly to her husband in such a way / that the senior wife herself, even if unwilling, would place her in authority as if by force.

1.14.s:
sāpi vijñāya bhartāraṃ kaniṣṭhākṛṣṭamānasam .
viśrāmaṃ prārthayedenāmadhikuryātsutāmiva . . 24
1.14.d:
सापि विज्ञाय भर्तारं कनिष्ठाकृष्टमानसम् ।
विश्रामं प्रार्थयेदेनामधिकुर्यात्सुतामिव ॥ 24
1.14.m: She too, realizing that her husband's mind is attracted to the junior wife, / should ask her for rest and place her in charge like a daughter.

1.14.s:
matvā bharturabhipretaṃ rakṣantī nijagauravam .
kṛtaṃ bhartranukūlaṃ syāttadiṣṭāyānumodayet . . 25
1.14.d:
मत्वा भर्तुरभिप्रेतं रक्षन्ती निजगौरवम् ।
कृतं भर्त्रनुकूलं स्यात्तदिष्टायानुमोदयेत् ॥ 25
1.14.m: Knowing her husband's intention and protecting her own dignity, / whatever is done should be pleasing to her husband, and she should approve what he desires.

1.14.s:
sthānino yadabhipretaṃ bhṛtyaiḥ kiṃ kriyate'nyathā .
kliśyate tatra mūḍhātmā paratantro vṛthā janaḥ . . 26
1.14.d:
स्थानिनो यदभिप्रेतं भृत्यैः किं क्रियतेऽन्यथा ।
क्लिश्यते तत्र मूढात्मा परतन्त्रो वृथा जनः ॥ 26
1.14.m: What can servants do contrary to what is intended by the master? / In that matter, the foolish, dependent person suffers in vain.

1.14.s:
tasmātsarvāsvavasthāsu manovākkāyakarmabhiḥ .
hitaṃ svāmyanukūlatvaṃ nārīṇāṃ tu viśeṣataḥ . . 27
1.14.d:
तस्मात्सर्वास्ववस्थासु मनोवाक्कायकर्मभिः ।
हितं स्वाम्यनुकूलत्वं नारीणां तु विशेषतः ॥ 27
1.14.m: Therefore, in all circumstances, by acts of mind, speech, and body, / conformity to one's master is beneficial, especially for women.

1.14.s:
sāpi jyeṣṭhāpatiṃ caiva gṛhatantraṃ ca sarvadā .
samāvarjya 1 guṇairdhīrā prāgavasthāṃ na vismaret . . 28
1.14.d:
सापि ज्येष्ठापतिं चैव गृहतन्त्रं च सर्वदा ।
समावर्ज्य 1 गुणैर्धीरा प्रागवस्थां न विस्मरेत् ॥ 28
1.14.m: She too, the steadfast woman, having won over the senior wife, her husband, and the household order at all times / by her virtues, should not forget her former condition.

1.14.s:
na saubhāgyamadaṃ kuryānna cauddhatyādivikriyām .
nitarāmānatiṃ gacchetsadānāryabhayādiva . . 29
1.14.d:
न सौभाग्यमदं कुर्यान्न चौद्धत्यादिविक्रियाम् ।
नितरामानतिं गच्छेत्सदानार्यभयादिव ॥ 29
1.14.m: She should not exhibit pride in good fortune, nor aberration such as arrogance; / she should thoroughly maintain humility, as if always in fear of an ignoble act.

1.14.s:
yathā yogyatayā patyau saubhāgyamabhivardhate .
spardhayecya kulastrīṇāṃ praśrayopādhikaṃ tathā . . 1.14.30
1.14.d:
यथा योग्यतया पत्यौ सौभाग्यमभिवर्धते ।
स्पर्धयेच्य कुलस्त्रीणां प्रश्रयोपाधिकं तथा ॥ 1.14.30
1.14.m: Just as good fortune with her husband increases through fitness, / so emulation among highborn women has modesty as its condition.

1.14.s:
evamārādhya bhartāraṃ tatkāryeṣvapramādinī .
pūjyānāṃ pūjane nityaṃ bhṛtyānāṃ bharaṇeṣu ca . . 31
1.14.d:
एवमाराध्य भर्तारं तत्कार्येष्वप्रमादिनी ।
पूज्यानां पूजने नित्यं भृत्यानां भरणेषु च ॥ 31
1.14.m: Having thus gratified her husband, being vigilant in his affairs, / always in honoring those worthy of honor and in maintaining servants,

1.14.s:
guṇānāmarjane nityaṃ śīlavatparirakṣaṇe .
pretya ceha ca nirdvandvaṃ sukhamāpnotyanuttamam . . 32
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi strīdharmeṣu
sapatnīkartavyavarṇanaṃ nāma caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ . 14 .
strīdharmavarṇanam
1.14.d:
गुणानामर्जने नित्यं शीलवत्परिरक्षणे ।
प्रेत्य चेह च निर्द्वन्द्वं सुखमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥ 32
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि स्त्रीधर्मेषु
सपत्नीकर्तव्यवर्णनं नाम चतुर्दशोऽध्यायः । 14 ।
स्त्रीधर्मवर्णनम्
1.14.m:
in constantly acquiring virtues, and in guarding [herself] like a virtuous woman, / she attains unsurpassed, unconflicted happiness here and in the hereafter.
Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Duties of Co-wives', in the duties of women, in the Brāhmaparvan of the venerable Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa containing fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Duties of Women

1.15.s:
brahmovāca
durbhagā ca punarnityamupavāsāditatparā .
bāhyeṣu patikṛtyeṣu syādviśeṣābhiyoginī . . 1
1.15.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
दुर्भगा च पुनर्नित्यमुपवासादितत्परा ।
बाह्येषु पतिकृत्येषु स्याद्विशेषाभियोगिनी ॥ 1
1.15.m: Brahmā said: / Moreover, an unfortunate woman, constantly intent upon fasts and the like, / should be especially engaged in external tasks for her husband.

1.15.s:
na praśaṃsāṃ sapatnīṣu niṃdāṃ cāpi tathātmani .
asūyāṃ bharturīrṣyāṃ vā praṇayaṃ vāpi darśayet . . 2
1.15.d:
न प्रशंसां सपत्नीषु निंदां चापि तथात्मनि ।
असूयां भर्तुरीर्ष्यां वा प्रणयं वापि दर्शयेत् ॥ 2
1.15.m: She should not display praise among co-wives, nor censure of herself; / nor should she display malice, jealousy toward her husband, or affection.

1.15.s:
madvidhā yā hi bahvetattaccāttyaṃtikamaśnute .
yadasyā yuṣmato yāyādbhāryāśabdābhidheyatām . . 3
1.15.d:
मद्विधा या हि बह्वेतत्तच्चात्त्यंतिकमश्नुते ।
यदस्या युष्मतो यायाद्भार्याशब्दाभिधेयताम् ॥ 3
1.15.m: Indeed, someone like me attains this abundance, and that exceedingly, / because she may attain the designation of 'wife' to one as long-lived as you.

1.15.s:
na ca nirbhūṣaṇā tiṣṭhenna cāpyuddhatabhūṣaṇā .
nānyadā gaṃdhamālyādi grāhyaṃ patyupacārataḥ . . 4
1.15.d:
न च निर्भूषणा तिष्ठेन्न चाप्युद्धतभूषणा ।
नान्यदा गंधमाल्यादि ग्राह्यं पत्युपचारतः ॥ 4
1.15.m: She should neither remain without ornaments, nor should she wear haughty ornaments; / at other times perfumes, garlands, and the like should not be taken, except when serving her husband.

1.15.s:
tannyūnaṃ sarvaśo grāhyaṃ vallabhāyā viśeṣataḥ .
bhūṣaṇaṃ gandhamālyaṃ tu tāvatkālamalakṣitam . . 5
1.15.d:
तन्न्यूनं सर्वशो ग्राह्यं वल्लभाया विशेषतः ।
भूषणं गन्धमाल्यं तु तावत्कालमलक्षितम् ॥ 5
1.15.m: She should take altogether less than the favorite wife in particular; / an ornament, perfume, or garland, however, should remain unperceived for that duration of time.

1.15.s:
sambādhānāṃ pradeśānāṃ nityaṃ svedādimārjanam .
dantanāsādipaṅkānāṃ vigandhasya ca śodhanam . . 6
1.15.d:
सम्बाधानां प्रदेशानां नित्यं स्वेदादिमार्जनम् ।
दन्तनासादिपङ्कानां विगन्धस्य च शोधनम् ॥ 6
1.15.m: Daily wiping of sweat and the like from the private parts, / and cleansing of grime from teeth, nose, and the like, and of bad odors [should be done].

1.15.s:
nimittaṃ bharturetāsāṃ yatkiṃcidabhilakṣayet .
nānena vā tayoryatnaṃ vidadhyādaṅgamārjane . . 7
1.15.d:
निमित्तं भर्तुरेतासां यत्किंचिदभिलक्षयेत् ।
नानेन वा तयोर्यत्नं विदध्यादङ्गमार्जने ॥ 7
1.15.m: Whatever sign of these the husband might notice, / by no means should she make an effort to cleanse her body in their presence.

1.15.s:
sarvāsāṃ ca sapatnīnāṃ sarvatrānugatā bhavet .
vaitasīṃ vṛttimāsthāya vallabhāyā viśeṣataḥ . . 8
1.15.d:
सर्वासां च सपत्नीनां सर्वत्रानुगता भवेत् ।
वैतसीं वृत्तिमास्थाय वल्लभाया विशेषतः ॥ 8
1.15.m: And toward all co-wives she should be compliant in every way, / adopting the conduct of a reed, especially toward the favorite wife.

1.15.s:
anyasyā yadanuṣṭheyaṃ yanna sīdetsamarpitam .
bhartuścāviditaṃ yatnāttatkuryādavirodhi cet . . 9
1.15.d:
अन्यस्या यदनुष्ठेयं यन्न सीदेत्समर्पितम् ।
भर्तुश्चाविदितं यत्नात्तत्कुर्यादविरोधि चेत् ॥ 9
1.15.m: Whatever is to be performed for another that would not suffer if entrusted, / she should perform with effort without her husband's knowledge, if it causes no conflict.

1.15.s:
kośavastrānnatāmbūlagandhāpānauṣadhādikam .
tatsarvamaniyuktānāṃ doṣavatvādvirudhyate . . 1.15.10
1.15.d:
कोशवस्त्रान्नताम्बूलगन्धापानौषधादिकम् ।
तत्सर्वमनियुक्तानां दोषवत्वाद्विरुध्यते ॥ 1.15.10
1.15.m: Treasury, clothes, food, betel, perfumes, drinks, medicines, and the like— / all that is objectionable for those not authorized, because it involves fault.

1.15.s:
yattu muktamanuṣṭheyaṃ gahasammārjanādikam .
strīṇāmanadhikāre'pi prāyastadvidhirucyate . . 11
1.15.d:
यत्तु मुक्तमनुष्ठेयं गहसम्मार्जनादिकम् ।
स्त्रीणामनधिकारेऽपि प्रायस्तद्विधिरुच्यते ॥ 11
1.15.m: However, that which is left to be performed, such as sweeping the house, / is generally prescribed as a duty for women even when they have no formal authority.

1.15.s:
abhyaṅgodvartanaṃ snānaṃ bhojanaṃ maṇḍanāni ca .
kuryādbharturapatyānāṃ dhātrīkarmāṇi sādaram . . 12
1.15.d:
अभ्यङ्गोद्वर्तनं स्नानं भोजनं मण्डनानि च ।
कुर्याद्भर्तुरपत्यानां धात्रीकर्माणि सादरम् ॥ 12
1.15.m: Inunction, rubbing with fragrant paste, bathing, food, and ornamentation— / she should respectfully perform the duties of a nurse for the husband's children.

1.15.s:
ātmavattānyapatyāni sādhayatyanuyogataḥ .
svenāpyamīṣāṃ vittena vidadhyānmaṇḍanādikam . . 13
1.15.d:
आत्मवत्तान्यपत्यानि साधयत्यनुयोगतः ।
स्वेनाप्यमीषां वित्तेन विदध्यान्मण्डनादिकम् ॥ 13
1.15.m: She manages the children like her own through attentive care; / she should provide ornaments and the like for them even with her own wealth.

1.15.s:
bhogaḥ svayamapatyairvā strīvittasya patirvidhā .
pūrve vayasyabhinandya paścime copayojanam . . 14
1.15.d:
भोगः स्वयमपत्यैर्वा स्त्रीवित्तस्य पतिर्विधा ।
पूर्वे वयस्यभिनन्द्य पश्चिमे चोपयोजनम् ॥ 14
1.15.m: The enjoyment of a woman's wealth is by herself, by the children, or by the husband; / its utilization is to be welcomed in the earlier age and in the later.

1.15.s:
ubhayogastu vā mā vā karmajaḥ pṛthageva saḥ .
sadvṛtte tvadhikāṃ khyātiṃ kurvīta kriyayā punaḥ . . 15
1.15.d:
उभयोगस्तु वा मा वा कर्मजः पृथगेव सः ।
सद्वृत्ते त्वधिकां ख्यातिं कुर्वीत क्रियया पुनः ॥ 15
1.15.m: Whether there is use of both or not, it arises from past action and is distinct; / in good conduct, however, she should make higher renown again through her deeds.

1.15.s:
na kāpi durbhagā nāma subhagā nāma jātitaḥ .
vyavahārādbhavatyeṣa nirdeśo ripumitravat . . 16
1.15.d:
न कापि दुर्भगा नाम सुभगा नाम जातितः ।
व्यवहाराद्भवत्येष निर्देशो रिपुमित्रवत् ॥ 16
1.15.m: No woman is called unfortunate or fortunate merely by birth; / this designation arises from behavior, like 'enemy' or 'friend'.

1.15.s:
bhartṛcittāparijñānādananuṣṭhānato'pi vā.
vṛttairlokaviruddhaiśca yānti durbhagatāṃ striyaḥ . . 17
1.15.d:
भर्तृचित्तापरिज्ञानादननुष्ठानतोऽपि वा।
वृत्तैर्लोकविरुद्धैश्च यान्ति दुर्भगतां स्त्रियः ॥ 17
1.15.m: From failure to understand their husband's mind, or from non-performance [of duties], / and through conduct contrary to the world, women arrive at the state of being unloved.

1.15.s:
prānukūlyānmanovṛttaiḥ paro'pi priyatāṃ vrajet .
prātikūlyānnijopyāśu priyaḥ pradveṣatāmiyāt . . 18
1.15.d:
प्रानुकूल्यान्मनोवृत्तैः परोऽपि प्रियतां व्रजेत् ।
प्रातिकूल्यान्निजोप्याशु प्रियः प्रद्वेषतामियात् ॥ 18
1.15.m: Through compliance of mental disposition, even a stranger may become beloved; / through contrariness, even one's own dear person quickly attains enmity.

1.15.s:
tasmātsarvāsvavasthāsu manovākkāyakarmabhiḥ .
priyaṃ samācarennityaṃ taccitānuvidhāyinī . . 19
1.15.d:
तस्मात्सर्वास्ववस्थासु मनोवाक्कायकर्मभिः ।
प्रियं समाचरेन्नित्यं तच्चितानुविधायिनी ॥ 19
1.15.m: Therefore, in all circumstances, by acts of mind, speech, and body, / she should constantly act pleasantly, conforming to his mind.

1.15.s:
yāmanyāṃ kāmayettāsāṃ taṃ tayā saṃprayojayet .
kupitāṃ ca priyāṃ kāñcidyatnādasmai prasādayet . . 1.15.20
1.15.d:
यामन्यां कामयेत्तासां तं तया संप्रयोजयेत् ।
कुपितां च प्रियां काञ्चिद्यत्नादस्मै प्रसादयेत् ॥ 1.15.20
1.15.m: Whichever other [co-wife] among them he desires, she should unite him with her; / and if a certain beloved wife is angry, she should diligently conciliate her for him.

1.15.s:
tatpādaparicaryāyāṃ gotrasaṃvāhane 1 tathā .
pīḍane śirasaścaiva paraṃ kauśalamabhyaset . . 21
1.15.d:
तत्पादपरिचर्यायां गोत्रसंवाहने 1 तथा ।
पीडने शिरसश्चैव परं कौशलमभ्यसेत् ॥ 21
1.15.m: In attending to his feet, in massaging his limbs, / and in pressing his head, she should cultivate the utmost skill.

1.15.s:
pīḍanaṃ mṛdu madhyaṃ ca gātrāvasthāviśeṣataḥ .
mukhagātrādibhirliṅgaiḥ prayojyaṃ tatsukhāvaham . . 22
1.15.d:
पीडनं मृदु मध्यं च गात्रावस्थाविशेषतः ।
मुखगात्रादिभिर्लिङ्गैः प्रयोज्यं तत्सुखावहम् ॥ 22
1.15.m: Pressing may be soft or moderate, according to the specific condition of his limbs; / it should be applied so as to bring comfort, judging by indications from the face, limbs, and the like.

1.15.s:
bāhūrukaṭipṛṣṭheṣu skaṃdhe śirasi pādayoḥ .
gāḍhamardanamicchanti prāyonyatrāpi madhyamam . . 23
1.15.d:
बाहूरुकटिपृष्ठेषु स्कंधे शिरसि पादयोः ।
गाढमर्दनमिच्छन्ति प्रायोन्यत्रापि मध्यमम् ॥ 23
1.15.m: On the arms, thighs, hips, back, shoulders, head, and feet, / they desire firm rubbing; generally elsewhere, moderate.

1.15.s:
nirmāṃseṣu pradeśeṣu nābhimūleṣu marmasu .
hṛdgaṇḍakakapolādāvicchanti mṛdumardanam . . 24
1.15.d:
निर्मांसेषु प्रदेशेषु नाभिमूलेषु मर्मसु ।
हृद्गण्डककपोलादाविच्छन्ति मृदुमर्दनम् ॥ 24
1.15.m: On fleshless parts, at the base of the navel, on vital points, / on the chest, temple, and cheek, they desire soft rubbing.

1.15.s:
gāḍhaṃ jāgradavasthāyāmardhasuptasya madhyamam .
kiñcitsaparighātaṃ ca mṛdusuptasya neti vā . . 25
1.15.d:
गाढं जाग्रदवस्थायामर्धसुप्तस्य मध्यमम् ।
किञ्चित्सपरिघातं च मृदुसुप्तस्य नेति वा ॥ 25
1.15.m: Firm [pressure] during the waking state, moderate for one half-asleep / with gentle patting, and soft for one asleep—or not at all.

1.15.s:
viruddhaṃ sarvagātreṣu2 lomavastu viśeṣataḥ .
utkaṇḍūyatyu soddharṣaṃ snehākteṣu ca marda nam . . 26
1.15.d:
विरुद्धं सर्वगात्रेषु2 लोमवस्तु विशेषतः ।
उत्कण्डूयत्यु सोद्धर्षं स्नेहाक्तेषु च मर्द नम् ॥ 26
1.15.m: It is improper on all limbs, especially on hairy areas, / to scratch violently with friction, and to rub upon parts smeared with oil.

1.15.s:
sparśādromāñcajananaṃ sanakhacchuritaṃ śanaiḥ .
pulakollekhanopetaṃ śiraḥkaṃḍūśca pārśvayoḥ . . 27
1.15.d:
स्पर्शाद्रोमाञ्चजननं सनखच्छुरितं शनैः ।
पुलकोल्लेखनोपेतं शिरःकंडूश्च पार्श्वयोः ॥ 27
1.15.m: Causing horripilation by touch, gently tracing with nails, / accompanying the bristling of hair, and scratching the head on both sides [should be done].

1.15.s:
teṣu teṣu ca gātreṣu tatprayojyaṃ tathātathā .
nidrāgamāya tatkāle rāgasaṃdhukṣaṇāya ca . . 28
1.15.d:
तेषु तेषु च गात्रेषु तत्प्रयोज्यं तथातथा ।
निद्रागमाय तत्काले रागसंधुक्षणाय च ॥ 28
1.15.m: And on those various limbs, it should be applied in that manner, / to bring on sleep at that time and to kindle passion.

1.15.s:
tiṣṭhataścopaviṣṭasya 1 jāgrataḥ svapato'pi vā .
saṃvāhanaṃ praśaṃsaṃti yadatyarthaṃ sukhāvaham . . 29
1.15.d:
तिष्ठतश्चोपविष्टस्य 1 जाग्रतः स्वपतोऽपि वा ।
संवाहनं प्रशंसंति यदत्यर्थं सुखावहम् ॥ 29
1.15.m: Whether he is standing, seated, awake, or even asleep, / they praise massage because it brings extraordinary pleasure.

1.15.s:
naiṣpandyaṃ pulakodbhedo gātrāṇāmakṣimīlanam .
tatpradeśārpaṇaṃ kiñcidbodhedvikṛtidarśanam . . 1.15.30
1.15.d:
नैष्पन्द्यं पुलकोद्भेदो गात्राणामक्षिमीलनम् ।
तत्प्रदेशार्पणं किञ्चिद्बोधेद्विकृतिदर्शनम् ॥ 1.15.30
1.15.m: Motionlessness, the bristling of body hair, the closing of the eyes, / presenting that part [of the body], perceiving some slight alteration [of mood]—

1.15.s:
ūrū mūlādideśe ca tatpāṇipratipīḍanam .
lakṣayennipuṇā2 yatra tatraivādhikamācaret . . 31
1.15.d:
ऊरू मूलादिदेशे च तत्पाणिप्रतिपीडनम् ।
लक्षयेन्निपुणा2 यत्र तत्रैवाधिकमाचरेत् ॥ 31
1.15.m: on the thighs and the region of the groin, pressing with his hand: / wherever the clever woman notices this, there she should do more.

1.15.s:
evameva yathoddiṣṭaṃ strīvṛttaṃ yānutiṣṭhati .
patimārādhya sampūrṇa trivargaṃ sādhigacchati3 . . 32
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi strīdharmavarṇanaṃ
nāma paṃcadaśo'dhyāyaḥ . 15 .
pratipatkalpavarṇanam
1.15.d:
एवमेव यथोद्दिष्टं स्त्रीवृत्तं यानुतिष्ठति ।
पतिमाराध्य सम्पूर्ण त्रिवर्गं साधिगच्छति3 ॥ 32
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि स्त्रीधर्मवर्णनं
नाम पंचदशोऽध्यायः । 15 ।
प्रतिपत्कल्पवर्णनम्
1.15.m:
She who carries out women's conduct in this manner as instructed, / worshipping her husband, attains the complete trivarga.
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, named “The Description of the Duties of Women,” in the Brāhmaparvan of the venerable Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the recension of fifty thousand verses.
Description of the Rite of the First Lunar Day

1.16.s:
sumanturuvāca
ityuktvā bhagavānbrahmā strīlakṣaṇamaśeṣataḥ .
sadvṛttaṃ ca tathā strīṇāṃ jagāma sa nijālayam . . 1
1.16.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान्ब्रह्मा स्त्रीलक्षणमशेषतः ।
सद्वृत्तं च तथा स्त्रीणां जगाम स निजालयम् ॥ 1
1.16.m: Sumantu said: / Having thus fully explained the bodily characteristics of women / and the virtuous conduct of women, the Lord Brahmā departed for his own abode.

1.16.s:
ṛṣayaśca tathā jagmuḥ svāni dhiṣṇyānyaśeṣataḥ .
strīlakṣaṇaṃ tathā vṛttaṃ śrutvā kṛtsnaṃ mahīpate . . 2
1.16.d:
ऋषयश्च तथा जग्मुः स्वानि धिष्ण्यान्यशेषतः ।
स्त्रीलक्षणं तथा वृत्तं श्रुत्वा कृत्स्नं महीपते ॥ 2
1.16.m: And likewise the sages, having heard in full the characteristics of women / and their conduct, went to their respective seats, O king.

1.16.s:
itthaṃ lakṣaṇasampannāṃ bhāryāṃ prāpya mahīpate .
kartavyaṃ yadgṛhasthena tadidānīṃ nibodha me . . 3
1.16.d:
इत्थं लक्षणसम्पन्नां भार्यां प्राप्य महीपते ।
कर्तव्यं यद्गृहस्थेन तदिदानीं निबोध मे ॥ 3
1.16.m: Having obtained a wife endowed with such characteristics, O king, / learn now from me what the householder must do.

1.16.s:
baivāhikāgnau kurvīta gṛhyaṃ karma yathāvidhi .
pañcayajñavidhānaṃ tu paktiṃ kuryātsadā gṛhī . .4
1.16.d:
बैवाहिकाग्नौ कुर्वीत गृह्यं कर्म यथाविधि ।
पञ्चयज्ञविधानं तु पक्तिं कुर्यात्सदा गृही ॥4
1.16.m: In the nuptial fire he should perform the domestic ritual according to rule, / and the householder should constantly cook according to the rule of the five sacrifices.

1.16.s:
pañca sūnā gṛhasthasya tena svargaṃ na gacchati .
kaṇḍanī peṣaṇī cullī udakumbhīḥ pramārjanī . . 5
1.16.d:
पञ्च सूना गृहस्थस्य तेन स्वर्गं न गच्छति ।
कण्डनी पेषणी चुल्ली उदकुम्भीः प्रमार्जनी ॥ 5
1.16.m: The householder has five slaughterhouses, by which he does not go to heaven: / the pestle, the grindstone, the hearth, the water pot, and the broom.

1.16.s:
āsāṃ krameṇa sarvāsāṃ viśuddhyarthaṃ manīṣibhiḥ .
pañcoddiṣṭā mahāyajñāḥ pratyahaṃ gṛhamedhinām . . 6
1.16.d:
आसां क्रमेण सर्वासां विशुद्ध्यर्थं मनीषिभिः ।
पञ्चोद्दिष्टा महायज्ञाः प्रत्यहं गृहमेधिनाम् ॥ 6
1.16.m: For the gradual purification of all of these, wise men / have prescribed five great sacrifices daily for householders:

1.16.s:
adhyāpanaṃ brahmayajñaḥ pitṛyajñaśca tarpaṇam .
homo daivo balirbhaumastathānyo'tithipūjanam . .7
1.16.d:
अध्यापनं ब्रह्मयज्ञः पितृयज्ञश्च तर्पणम् ।
होमो दैवो बलिर्भौमस्तथान्योऽतिथिपूजनम् ॥7
1.16.m: teaching is the sacrifice to Brahman, libation is the sacrifice to the ancestors, / oblation into the fire is to the gods, an offering cast on the ground is to the beings, and the other is honouring guests.

1.16.s:
pañcaitānyo mahāyajñānna hāpayati śaktitaḥ .
sa gṛhe'pi vasannityaṃ sūnodorṣairna lipyate . . 8
1.16.d:
पञ्चैतान्यो महायज्ञान्न हापयति शक्तितः ।
स गृहेऽपि वसन्नित्यं सूनोदोर्षैर्न लिप्यते ॥ 8
1.16.m: He who does not neglect these five great sacrifices according to his capacity / is not tainted by the faults of the slaughterhouses, even though constantly dwelling in a house.

1.16.s:
devatātithibhṛtyānāṃ pitṝṇāmātmanaśca yaḥ .
na nirvapati pañcānāmucchvasanna ca jīvati . . 9
1.16.d:
देवतातिथिभृत्यानां पितॄणामात्मनश्च यः ।
न निर्वपति पञ्चानामुच्छ्वसन्न च जीवति ॥ 9
1.16.m: He who does not offer [portions] to these five— / to the deities, guests, servants, ancestors, and himself—breathes, but does not live.

1.16.s:
śatānīka uvāca
yasya nāsti gṛhe tvagniḥ sa mṛto nātra saṃśayaḥ .
na sa pūjayituṃ śakto devādīnbrāhmaṇottamaḥ . . 1.16.10
1.16.d:
शतानीक उवाच
यस्य नास्ति गृहे त्वग्निः स मृतो नात्र संशयः ।
न स पूजयितुं शक्तो देवादीन्ब्राह्मणोत्तमः ॥ 1.16.10
1.16.m: Śatānīka said: / He in whose house there is no fire is dead, there is no doubt of this; / he is not capable of worshipping the gods and other beings, O best of brahmins.

1.16.s:
niragnikasya viprasya kathaṃ devādayo dvija. .
prītāḥ syuḥ śāntaye tasya paraṃ kautūhalaṃ mama . . 11
1.16.d:
निरग्निकस्य विप्रस्य कथं देवादयो द्विज॥
प्रीताः स्युः शान्तये तस्य परं कौतूहलं मम ॥ 11
1.16.m: How can the gods and other beings be pleased with a brahmin without a fire / for his welfare, O twice-born? Great is my curiosity.

1.16.s:
sumanturuvāca
sādhu pṛṣṭo'smi rājendra śrūyatāṃ paramaṃ vacaḥ.
anagnayastu ye viprāsteṣāṃ śreyo'bhidhīyate . . 12
1.16.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
साधु पृष्टोऽस्मि राजेन्द्र श्रूयतां परमं वचः।
अनग्नयस्तु ये विप्रास्तेषां श्रेयोऽभिधीयते ॥ 12
1.16.m: Sumantu said: / I am well questioned, O king of kings; listen to the supreme teaching. / The welfare of those brahmins who are without fires is explained [here].

1.16.s:
vratopavāsaniyamairnānādānaistathā 1 nṛpa .
devādayo bhavantyeva prītāsteṣāṃ na saṃśayaḥ . . 13
1.16.d:
व्रतोपवासनियमैर्नानादानैस्तथा 1 नृप ।
देवादयो भवन्त्येव प्रीतास्तेषां न संशयः ॥ 13
1.16.m: By observances, fasts, and restraints, and likewise by various gifts, O king, / the gods and other beings indeed become pleased with them, of this there is no doubt.

1.16.s:
viśeṣādupavāsena tithau kila mahīpate .
prītā devādayasteṣāṃ bhavanti kurunandana . . 14
1.16.d:
विशेषादुपवासेन तिथौ किल महीपते ।
प्रीता देवादयस्तेषां भवन्ति कुरुनन्दन ॥ 14
1.16.m: Especially through fasting on a lunar day, O king, / the gods and other beings become pleased with them, O delight of the Kurus.

1.16.s:
śatānīka uvāca
bhagavaṃstvaṃ tithīnbrūhi tithīnāṃ ca vidhiṃ hi me .
prāśanaṃ gṛhyadharmāṃśca upavāsavidhīnapi . . 15
1.16.d:
शतानीक उवाच
भगवंस्त्वं तिथीन्ब्रूहि तिथीनां च विधिं हि मे ।
प्राशनं गृह्यधर्मांश्च उपवासविधीनपि ॥ 15
1.16.m: Śatānīka said: / O venerable one, tell me the lunar days and the rule for the lunar days, / the consumption of foods, domestic duties, and also the rules of fasting,

1.16.s:
mucyema yena pāpaughāttvatprasāddvijottama .
saṃsārāccāpi viprendra śreyase jagatastathā . . 16
1.16.d:
मुच्येम येन पापौघात्त्वत्प्रसाद्द्विजोत्तम ।
संसाराच्चापि विप्रेन्द्र श्रेयसे जगतस्तथा ॥ 16
1.16.m: by which we may be freed from the flood of sins through your grace, O best of the twice-born, / and from transmigration, O chief of brahmins, and also for the welfare of the world.

1.16.s:
sumanturuvāca
śṛṇu kaurava karmāṇi tithiguhyāśritāni tu .
śrutāni ghnanti pāpāni upoṣitaphalāni ca . . 17
1.16.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
शृणु कौरव कर्माणि तिथिगुह्याश्रितानि तु ।
श्रुतानि घ्नन्ति पापानि उपोषितफलानि च ॥ 17
1.16.m: Sumantu said: / Listen, O Kaurava, to the actions dependent on the secrets of the lunar days, / which, when heard, destroy sins, as well as the fruits of fasting.

1.16.s:
pratipadi kṣīraprāśanaṃ dvitīyāyāṃ lavaṇavarjanam .
tṛtīyāyāṃ tilānnaṃ prāśnīyāccaturthyāṃ kṣīrāśanaśca pañcamyām . .
phalāśanaḥ sadā ṣaṣṭhyāṃ śākāśanaḥ saptamyāṃ bilvāhāroṣṭamyāṃ tu . . 18
1.16.d:
प्रतिपदि क्षीरप्राशनं द्वितीयायां लवणवर्जनम् ।
तृतीयायां तिलान्नं प्राश्नीयाच्चतुर्थ्यां क्षीराशनश्च पञ्चम्याम् ॥
फलाशनः सदा षष्ठ्यां शाकाशनः सप्तम्यां बिल्वाहारोष्टम्यां तु ॥ 18
1.16.m: On the first lunar day, consumption of milk; on the second, abstention from salt; / on the third, one should consume sesamum-rice; on the fourth and fifth, eating milk; / on the sixth, always eating fruit; on the seventh, eating vegetables; on the eighth, an intake of bilva fruit;

1.16.s:
piṣṭāśano navamyāmanagnipākāhāro daśamyāmekādaśyāṃ ghṛtāhāro dvādaśyāṃ pāyasāhāraḥ .
trayodaśyāṃ gomūtrāhāraścaturdaśyāṃ yavānnāhāraḥ . . 19
1.16.d:
पिष्टाशनो नवम्यामनग्निपाकाहारो दशम्यामेकादश्यां घृताहारो द्वादश्यां पायसाहारः ।
त्रयोदश्यां गोमूत्राहारश्चतुर्दश्यां यवान्नाहारः ॥ 19
1.16.m: on the ninth, eating flour; on the tenth, eating food uncooked by fire; on the eleventh, eating ghee; on the twelfth, eating milk rice; / on the thirteenth, consuming cow urine; on the fourteenth, eating barley food;

1.16.s:
kuśodakaprāśanaḥ paurṇamāsyāṃ haviṣyāhāro'māvāsyāyām .
eṣa prāśanavidhistithīnāmeva cānena vidhinā pakṣamekaṃ yo vartayati . . 1.16.20
1.16.d:
कुशोदकप्राशनः पौर्णमास्यां हविष्याहारोऽमावास्यायाम् ।
एष प्राशनविधिस्तिथीनामेव चानेन विधिना पक्षमेकं यो वर्तयति ॥ 1.16.20
1.16.m: on the full moon, drinking kuśa water; on the new moon, eating sacrificial food. / This is the rule of consumption for the lunar days, and he who spends a single fortnight according to this rule

1.16.s:
so'śvamedhaphalaṃ daśaguṇaphalamavāpnoti .
svarge manvantarāṇi yāvatprativasati . . 21
1.16.d:
सोऽश्वमेधफलं दशगुणफलमवाप्नोति ।
स्वर्गे मन्वन्तराणि यावत्प्रतिवसति ॥ 21
1.16.m: attains tenfold the fruit of an horse sacrifice; / he dwells in heaven for manvantaras,

1.16.s:
upagīyamānopsarogandharvairmāsatrayacatuṣṭayam .
sośvamedharājasūyānāṃ śataguṇamavāpnoti . . 22
1.16.d:
उपगीयमानोप्सरोगन्धर्वैर्मासत्रयचतुष्टयम् ।
सोश्वमेधराजसूयानां शतगुणमवाप्नोति ॥ 22
1.16.m: celebrated in song by apsarases and gandharvas. [If he maintains this] for three or four months, / he attains a hundred times the fruit of the horse sacrifice and the royal consecration.

1.16.s:
svarge upagīyamānopsarogandharvaiścaturyugānāṃ daśaśatīryāvatprativasati .
tathāṣṭamāsapāraṇe rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ sahasraguṇaphalamavāpnoti . . 23
1.16.d:
स्वर्गे उपगीयमानोप्सरोगन्धर्वैश्चतुर्युगानां दशशतीर्यावत्प्रतिवसति ।
तथाष्टमासपारणे राजसूयाश्वमेधाभ्यां सहस्रगुणफलमवाप्नोति ॥ 23
1.16.m: Celebrated in song in heaven by apsarases and gandharvas, he dwells there for a thousand four-age cycles; / and by breaking his fast after eight months, he attains a thousand times the fruit of the royal consecration and the horse sacrifice.

1.16.s:
svarge caturdaśa manvatarāṇi yāvatprativasati .
upagīyamānopsarogandharvairya evaṃ niyamamāsthāya varṣamekaṃ vartayati . . 24
1.16.d:
स्वर्गे चतुर्दश मन्वतराणि यावत्प्रतिवसति ।
उपगीयमानोप्सरोगन्धर्वैर्य एवं नियममास्थाय वर्षमेकं वर्तयति ॥ 24
1.16.m: He dwells in heaven for fourteen manvantaras, / celebrated in song by apsarases and gandharvas. He who, undertaking such a restraint, spends one year

1.16.s: sa saviturloke kālaṃ manvantaraṃ prativasati . . 25
1.16.d: स सवितुर्लोके कालं मन्वन्तरं प्रतिवसति ॥ 25
1.16.m: dwells in the world of the sun for the period of a manvantara.

1.16.s: ya evaṃ niyamānrājannāśvayujanavamyāṃ māghamāsasya saptamyāṃ vaiśākhatṛtīyāyāṃ kārtikapaurṇamāsyāṃ tithivratāni gṛdṛṇāti brahmacārī gṛhastho vanastho nārī naro vā śūdraḥ prayatamānasaḥ dīrghāyuṣyaṃ savituḥ sālokyaṃ vrajati..26
1.16.d: य एवं नियमान्राजन्नाश्वयुजनवम्यां माघमासस्य सप्तम्यां वैशाखतृतीयायां कार्तिकपौर्णमास्यां तिथिव्रतानि गृदृणाति ब्रह्मचारी गृहस्थो वनस्थो नारी नरो वा शूद्रः प्रयतमानसः दीर्घायुष्यं सवितुः सालोक्यं व्रजति॥26
1.16.m: Whoever, with subdued mind, undertakes these observances of the lunar days in this way, O king—on the ninth of Āśvayuja, the seventh of the month of Māgha, the third of Vaiśākha, and the full moon of Kārttika—whether a student of the Veda, a householder, a forest-dweller, a woman, a man, or a śūdra, attains long life and reaches the world of the sun.

1.16.s: yaiścāpi purā rājannanena vidhinā etāsu tithiṣvanyajanmāntare upavāsavidhiḥ kṛtaḥ dānāni dattāni vividhaprakārāṇi brāhmaṇānāṃ tapasvijaneṣu vā . . 27
1.16.d: यैश्चापि पुरा राजन्ननेन विधिना एतासु तिथिष्वन्यजन्मान्तरे उपवासविधिः कृतः दानानि दत्तानि विविधप्रकाराणि ब्राह्मणानां तपस्विजनेषु वा ॥ 27
1.16.m: And by those by whom in former times, O king, according to this rule, the rite of fasting was performed on these lunar days in another birth, and various kinds of gifts were given to brahmins or among ascetics,

1.16.s: trirātropavāsināṃ tīrthayātrātapogurumātāpitṛśuśrūśāniratānāṃ teṣāṃ svargādibhogavāsanādihāgatānāṃ phalaniṣpatticihnāni manuṣyaloke pratyakṣata eva dṛśyante . . 28
1.16.d: त्रिरात्रोपवासिनां तीर्थयात्रातपोगुरुमातापितृशुश्रूशानिरतानां तेषां स्वर्गादिभोगवासनादिहागतानां फलनिष्पत्तिचिह्नानि मनुष्यलोके प्रत्यक्षत एव दृश्यन्ते ॥ 28
1.16.m: or who fasted for three nights, being devoted to pilgrimages to sacred places, austerities, and service to their guru, mother, and father—for them, having arrived here after enjoying heaven and other realms, the marks of the accomplishment of fruits are visibly seen in the human world:

1.16.s: hastyaśvayānayugyadhanaratnakanakahiraṇyakaṭakakeyūragraiveyakakaṭisūtrakarṇālaṅkāramukuṭavaravastravaranārī-varavilepanasurūpaguṇadīrghāyuṣo vigatādhivyādhayo dānopavāsaratānāṃ phalānyetāni nṛtyagīta-vāditramaṅgalapāṭhakaśabdairihādyāpi puṇyakṛto bodhyamānā dṛśyanta iti . . 29
1.16.d: हस्त्यश्वयानयुग्यधनरत्नकनकहिरण्यकटककेयूरग्रैवेयककटिसूत्रकर्णालङ्कारमुकुटवरवस्त्रवरनारी-वरविलेपनसुरूपगुणदीर्घायुषो विगताधिव्याधयो दानोपवासरतानां फलान्येतानि नृत्यगीत-वादित्रमङ्गलपाठकशब्दैरिहाद्यापि पुण्यकृतो बोध्यमाना दृश्यन्त इति ॥ 29
1.16.m: elephants, horses, vehicles, draft animals, wealth, gems, gold, silver, bracelets, armlets, necklaces, waistbands, ear ornaments, diadems, excellent garments, excellent women, excellent unguents, handsome forms, virtues, long life, and freedom from mental distress and physical disease. These are the fruits of those devoted to gifts and fasts; even today those who have performed merit are seen here being awakened by the sounds of dances, songs, musical instruments, and auspicious panegyrists.

1.16.s: tathākṛtopavāsā api hi dṛśyante . . 1.16.30
1.16.d: तथाकृतोपवासा अपि हि दृश्यन्ते ॥ 1.16.30
1.16.m: Similarly, those who have observed fasts are indeed seen.

1.16.s: tathā adattadānā akṛtapuṇyāśca pratyakṣata eva dṛśyante . . 31
1.16.d: तथा अदत्तदाना अकृतपुण्याश्च प्रत्यक्षत एव दृश्यन्ते ॥ 31
1.16.m: Likewise, those who have given no gifts and performed no meritorious deeds are visibly seen:

1.16.s: tadyathā kāṇakuṣṭhibadhirajaḍamūkavyaṅgā rogadāridryopasargavyādhihatāyuṣaśca dṛśyaṃte'dyāpi mānavāḥ . . 32
1.16.d: तद्यथा काणकुष्ठिबधिरजडमूकव्यङ्गा रोगदारिद्र्योपसर्गव्याधिहतायुषश्च दृश्यंतेऽद्यापि मानवाः ॥ 32
1.16.m: namely, one-eyed, leprous, deaf, dull, mute, and deformed persons, struck down by disease, poverty, misfortune, illness, and a shortened lifespan—such men are seen even today.

1.16.s:
śatānīka uvāca
dvijendra tithayaḥ proktāḥ samāsena tvayā budha .
vistareṇaiva me bhūyaḥ prabrūhi dvijasattama . . 33
1.16.d:
शतानीक उवाच
द्विजेन्द्र तिथयः प्रोक्ताः समासेन त्वया बुध ।
विस्तरेणैव मे भूयः प्रब्रूहि द्विजसत्तम ॥ 33
1.16.m: Śatānīka said: / O chief of the twice-born, the lunar days have been declared by you in brief, O wise one. / Tell me [them] once more in detail, O best of the twice-born.

1.16.s:
rahasyaṃ yattithīnāṃ tu devānāṃ ca viceṣṭitam .
yānīṣṭāni ca devānāṃ bhojyāni niyamāstathā . . 34
1.16.d:
रहस्यं यत्तिथीनां तु देवानां च विचेष्टितम् ।
यानीष्टानि च देवानां भोज्यानि नियमास्तथा ॥ 34
1.16.m: The secret regarding the lunar days and the deeds of the gods, / and what foods are dear to the gods, as well as the restrictions,

1.16.s:
tāni me vada dharmajña yena pūto bhavenvaham .
nirdvandvo hi yathā vipra labhe yāgaphalāni tu . . 35
1.16.d:
तानि मे वद धर्मज्ञ येन पूतो भवेन्वहम् ।
निर्द्वन्द्वो हि यथा विप्र लभे यागफलानि तु ॥ 35
1.16.m: tell me those, O knower of dharma, so that I may become purified; / [and tell me] how, free from dualities, O brahmin, I may obtain the fruits of sacrifices.

1.16.s:
sumanturuvāca
rahasyaṃ yattithīnāṃ ca bhojanaṃ phalameva tu .
yāvacca yena niyamo viśeṣātstrījanasya ca . . 36
1.16.d:
सुमन्तुरुवाच
रहस्यं यत्तिथीनां च भोजनं फलमेव तु ।
यावच्च येन नियमो विशेषात्स्त्रीजनस्य च ॥ 36
1.16.m:
Sumantu said:
The secret regarding the lunar days, the food, and the fruit, / and the extent of the restriction by which [one acts], especially for womenfolk—

1.16.s:
etatte sarvamākhyāmo rahasyaṃ tannibodha me .
yanmayā noktapūrvaṃ hi kasyacitsupriyasya hi . . 37
1.16.d:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यामो रहस्यं तन्निबोध मे ।
यन्मया नोक्तपूर्वं हि कस्यचित्सुप्रियस्य हि ॥ 37
1.16.m: all that I shall declare to you; learn that secret from me, / which has never before been spoken by me even to anyone very dear.

1.16.s:
tatte'haṃ sampravakṣyāmi yasya devasya yā tithiḥ .
devatānāṃ rahasyāni vratāni niyamāstathā . . 38
1.16.d:
तत्तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि यस्य देवस्य या तिथिः ।
देवतानां रहस्यानि व्रतानि नियमास्तथा ॥ 38
1.16.m: I shall explain to you which lunar day belongs to which god, / the secrets of the deities, the votive observances, and the restrictions.

1.16.s:
tāñchṛṇuṣva mahābāho gadato mama nārada .
sṛṣṭiṃ pūrvaṃ vadiṣyāmi saṃkṣepeṇa tithiṃ prati . . 39
1.16.d:
ताञ्छृणुष्व महाबाहो गदतो मम नारद ।
सृष्टिं पूर्वं वदिष्यामि संक्षेपेण तिथिं प्रति ॥ 39
1.16.m: Hear them from me as I speak, O mighty-armed Nārada; / first I shall describe creation in brief with respect to the lunar day.

1.16.s:
tamobhūtamidaṃ tvāsīdalabhyamavitarkitam .
jagadbrahmā samāgatyāsṛjadātmānamātmanā . . 1.16.40
1.16.d:
तमोभूतमिदं त्वासीदलभ्यमवितर्कितम् ।
जगद्ब्रह्मा समागत्यासृजदात्मानमात्मना ॥ 1.16.40
1.16.m: This [universe] was enveloped in darkness, ungraspable, and unthinkable; / Brahmā, having assembled the world, created himself by himself.

1.16.s:
saṃbhūtātmaiva ātmāsāvaṇḍamadhyādviniḥsṛtaḥ .
ātmanaivātmano hyaṇḍaṃ sṛṣṭvā sa vibhurāditaḥ . . 41
1.16.d:
संभूतात्मैव आत्मासावण्डमध्याद्विनिःसृतः ।
आत्मनैवात्मनो ह्यण्डं सृष्ट्वा स विभुरादितः ॥ 41
1.16.m: Self-originated, that self came forth from the midst of the egg; / having created the egg of his own self by himself, that all-pervading lord at the beginning,

1.16.s:
brahmā nārāyaṇākhyo'sau sṛṣṭiṃ kartuṃ samudyataḥ .
tābhyāṃ soṇḍakapālābhyāṃ divaṃ bhūmiṃ ca nirmame . . 42
1.16.d:
ब्रह्मा नारायणाख्योऽसौ सृष्टिं कर्तुं समुद्यतः ।
ताभ्यां सोण्डकपालाभ्यां दिवं भूमिं च निर्ममे ॥ 42
1.16.m: Brahmā named Nārāyaṇa, set about to fashion the creation; / out of the two halves of that egg he formed heaven and earth,

1.16.s:
diśaścaivopadiśaścaiva devādīndānavāṃstathā .
tithiṃ pūrvāmimāṃ rājaṃścakārātha vibhuḥ svayam . . 43
1.16.d:
दिशश्चैवोपदिशश्चैव देवादीन्दानवांस्तथा ।
तिथिं पूर्वामिमां राजंश्चकाराथ विभुः स्वयम् ॥ 43
1.16.m: as well as the cardinal directions, intermediate directions, gods, and Dānavas; / then, O king, the all-pervading lord himself instituted this first lunar day.

1.16.s:
tithīnāṃ pravarā yasmādbrahmaṇā samudāhṛtā .
pratipāditā pare pūrve pratipattena tūcyate . . 44
1.16.d:
तिथीनां प्रवरा यस्माद्ब्रह्मणा समुदाहृता ।
प्रतिपादिता परे पूर्वे प्रतिपत्तेन तूच्यते ॥ 44
1.16.m: Because it was declared by Brahmā as the foremost of lunar days, / and was established before all others, it is therefore called pratipat.

1.16.s:
asmātpadāttu tithayo yasmāttvanyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ .
asyānte kathayiṣyāmi upavāsavidhiṃ param . . 45
1.16.d:
अस्मात्पदात्तु तिथयो यस्मात्त्वन्याः प्रकीर्तिताः ।
अस्यान्ते कथयिष्यामि उपवासविधिं परम् ॥ 45
1.16.m: Because the other lunar days are proclaimed from this foundation, / at its end I shall declare the supreme rule of fasting.

1.16.s:
kārttikyāṃ māghasaptamyāṃ vaiśākhasya yugādiṣu .
niyamopavāsaṃ prathamaṃ grāhayeta vidhānavit 1 . . 46
1.16.d:
कार्त्तिक्यां माघसप्तम्यां वैशाखस्य युगादिषु ।
नियमोपवासं प्रथमं ग्राहयेत विधानवित् 1 ॥ 46
1.16.m: On the full moon of Kārttika, on the seventh of Māgha, and at the beginnings of the yugas in Vaiśākha, / one who knows the ritual should first undertake the fast with restrictions.

1.16.s:
yāṃ tithiṃ niyamaṃ kartuṃ bhaktyā samanugacchati .
tasyāṃ tithau vidhānaṃ yattannibodha janādhipa . . 47
1.16.d:
यां तिथिं नियमं कर्तुं भक्त्या समनुगच्छति ।
तस्यां तिथौ विधानं यत्तन्निबोध जनाधिप ॥ 47
1.16.m: On whichever lunar day one faithfully undertakes the observance, / learn from me the ritual on that lunar day, O ruler of men.

1.16.s:
yadā tu pratipadyāṃ vai gṛhṇīyānniyamaṃ nṛpa .
caturdaśyāṃ kṛtāhāraḥ saṃkalpaṃ parikalpayet . . 48
1.16.d:
यदा तु प्रतिपद्यां वै गृह्णीयान्नियमं नृप ।
चतुर्दश्यां कृताहारः संकल्पं परिकल्पयेत् ॥ 48
1.16.m: When one takes up the observance on the pratipat, O king, / having eaten on the fourteenth, one should make the solemn resolve.

1.16.s:
amāvāsyāṃ na bhuñjīta trikālaṃ snānamācaret .
pavitro hi japennityaṃ gāyatrīṃ śirasā saha . . 49
1.16.d:
अमावास्यां न भुञ्जीत त्रिकालं स्नानमाचरेत् ।
पवित्रो हि जपेन्नित्यं गायत्रीं शिरसा सह ॥ 49
1.16.m: On the new moon day one must not eat; one should bathe at the three sandhyās; / purified, one should constantly recite the Gāyatrī together with its head.

1.16.s:
arcayitvā prabhāte tu gandhamālyairdvijottamān .
śaktyā kṣīraṃ pradadyāttu brahmā me prīyatāṃ prabhuḥ . . 1.16.50
1.16.d:
अर्चयित्वा प्रभाते तु गन्धमाल्यैर्द्विजोत्तमान् ।
शक्त्या क्षीरं प्रदद्यात्तु ब्रह्मा मे प्रीयतां प्रभुः ॥ 1.16.50
1.16.m: Having worshipped the best of brahmins at dawn with perfumes and garlands, / one should give milk according to one's means, [saying,] 'May Lord Brahmā be pleased with me.'

1.16.s:
tato bhuñjīta gokṣīramanena vidhinā nṛpa .
eṣa eva vidhirdṛṣṭaḥ sarvāsu tithiṣu nṛpa . . 51
1.16.d:
ततो भुञ्जीत गोक्षीरमनेन विधिना नृप ।
एष एव विधिर्दृष्टः सर्वासु तिथिषु नृप ॥ 51
1.16.m: Then one should consume cow's milk according to this rule, O king; / this very procedure is seen for all the lunar days, O king.

1.16.s:
saṃvatsaragate kāle vratametatsamāpyate .
vratāṃte yatphalaṃ tasya tannibodha narādhipa . . 52
1.16.d:
संवत्सरगते काले व्रतमेतत्समाप्यते ।
व्रतांते यत्फलं तस्य तन्निबोध नराधिप ॥ 52
1.16.m: When a year's time has passed, this votive observance is completed; / learn the fruit obtained at the conclusion of the votive observance, O ruler of men.

1.16.s:
vimuktapāpaḥ śuddhātmā divyadehasya dehinaḥ .
brahmā dadāti saṃtuṣṭo vimānamatitejasam . .
avyāhatagatiṃ divyaṃ kinnarāpsarasairyutam . . 53
1.16.d:
विमुक्तपापः शुद्धात्मा दिव्यदेहस्य देहिनः ।
ब्रह्मा ददाति संतुष्टो विमानमतितेजसम् ॥
अव्याहतगतिं दिव्यं किन्नराप्सरसैर्युतम् ॥ 53
1.16.m: Free from sin, pure in soul, for that embodied soul endowed with a divine body, / Brahmā, well-pleased, grants a celestial chariot of supreme splendour, / whose movement is unhindered, divine, accompanied by kinnaras and apsarases.

1.16.s:
ramitvā suciraṃ tatra daivataiḥ saha devavat .
iha cāgatya vipratvaṃ daśa janmānyasau labhet . . 54
1.16.d:
रमित्वा सुचिरं तत्र दैवतैः सह देववत् ।
इह चागत्य विप्रत्वं दश जन्मान्यसौ लभेत् ॥ 54
1.16.m: Having rejoiced there for a very long time with the gods like a god, / and having returned here, he attains brahminhood for ten births.

1.16.s:
vedavedāṃgavidyaśca dīrghāyuścaiva suprabhaḥ .
bhogī dhanapatirdātā jāyate'sau kṛte yuge . . 55
1.16.d:
वेदवेदांगविद्यश्च दीर्घायुश्चैव सुप्रभः ।
भोगी धनपतिर्दाता जायतेऽसौ कृते युगे ॥ 55
1.16.m: Learned in the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas, long-lived, and of great splendour, / an enjoyer of pleasures, a lord of wealth, and a donor, he is born in the Kṛta Yuga.

1.16.s:
viśvāmitrastu rājendra brāhmaṇatvajigīṣayā .
tapaścacāra vipulaṃ santāpāya divaukasām . .
brāhmaṇatvaṃ na lebhe'sau lebhe vighnānanekaśaḥ . . 56
1.16.d:
विश्वामित्रस्तु राजेन्द्र ब्राह्मणत्वजिगीषया ।
तपश्चचार विपुलं सन्तापाय दिवौकसाम् ॥
ब्राह्मणत्वं न लेभेऽसौ लेभे विघ्नाननेकशः ॥ 56
1.16.m: Viśvāmitra, O king of kings, desiring to attain brahminhood, / performed severe austerity to the torment of the denizens of heaven; / [yet] he did not obtain brahminhood, but obtained numerous obstacles.

1.16.s:
tatastu niyamātteṣāṃ tithīnāṃ pravarā tithiḥ .
upoṣitā bahuvidhā jñātvā brahmapriyāṃ tithim . . 57
1.16.d:
ततस्तु नियमात्तेषां तिथीनां प्रवरा तिथिः ।
उपोषिता बहुविधा ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मप्रियां तिथिम् ॥ 57
1.16.m: Then, through the discipline of these lunar days, the foremost lunar day, / dear to Brahmā, was fasted on in diverse ways once it was understood.

1.16.s:
tato dadau brahmā viśvāmitrāya dhīmate .
ihaiva tena dehena brāhmaṇatvaṃ sudurlabham . . 58
1.16.d:
ततो ददौ ब्रह्मा विश्वामित्राय धीमते ।
इहैव तेन देहेन ब्राह्मणत्वं सुदुर्लभम् ॥ 58
1.16.m: Then Brahmā granted to the wise Viśvāmitra, / in this very body and in this world, that brahminhood so very difficult to attain.

1.16.s:
tithīnāṃ pravarā hyeṣā tithīnāmuttamā tithiḥ .
kṣatriyo vaiśyaśūdrau vā brāhmaṇatvamavāpnuyuḥ . . 59
1.16.d:
तिथीनां प्रवरा ह्येषा तिथीनामुत्तमा तिथिः ।
क्षत्रियो वैश्यशूद्रौ वा ब्राह्मणत्वमवाप्नुयुः ॥ 59
1.16.m: This is indeed the foremost of lunar days, the best of lunar days; / through it a kṣatriya, a vaiśya, or a śūdra may attain brahminhood.

1.16.s:
evaṃ tithiriyaṃ rājankāmadā kañjajapriyā .
sarahasyā mayā proktā yā noktā yasya kasyacit . . 1.16.60
1.16.d:
एवं तिथिरियं राजन्कामदा कञ्जजप्रिया ।
सरहस्या मया प्रोक्ता या नोक्ता यस्य कस्यचित् ॥ 1.16.60
1.16.m: Thus this lunar day, granter of desires and dear to the lotus-born, / has been declared by me together with its secret, which has never been told to just anyone.

1.16.s:
haihayaistālajaṅghaiśca turuṣkairyavanaiḥ śakaiḥ .
upoṣitā ihātraiva brāhmaṇatvamabhīpsubhiḥ 1 . . 61
1.16.d:
हैहयैस्तालजङ्घैश्च तुरुष्कैर्यवनैः शकैः ।
उपोषिता इहात्रैव ब्राह्मणत्वमभीप्सुभिः 1 ॥ 61
1.16.m: It was fasted on right here by the Haihayas, Tālajaṅghas, / Turuṣkas, Yavanas, and Śakas, desiring to attain brahminhood.

1.16.s:
ityeṣā paramā puṇyā śivā pāpaharā tathā .
paṭhitopāsitā rājañchraddhayā ca śrutā 1 tathā . . 62
1.16.d:
इत्येषा परमा पुण्या शिवा पापहरा तथा ।
पठितोपासिता राजञ्छ्रद्धया च श्रुता 1 तथा ॥ 62
1.16.m: Thus, this [lunar day] is supremely auspicious, benign, and sin-destroying; / recited, venerated, O king, and heard with faith,

1.16.s:
māhātmyaṃ cāpi yopyasyāḥ śṛṇuyānmānavo nṛpa .
ṛddhiṃ vṛddhiṃ tathā kīrtiṃ śivaṃ cāpya divaṃ vrajet . . 63
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe śatārddhasāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ brāhme parvaṇi pratipatkalpavarṇanaṃ
nāma ṣoḍaśo'dhyāyaḥ . 16 .
1.16.d:
माहात्म्यं चापि योप्यस्याः शृणुयान्मानवो नृप ।
ऋद्धिं वृद्धिं तथा कीर्तिं शिवं चाप्य दिवं व्रजेत् ॥ 63
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे शतार्द्धसाहस्र्यां संहितायां ब्राह्मे पर्वणि प्रतिपत्कल्पवर्णनं
नाम षोडशोऽध्यायः । 16 ।
1.16.m:
and whatever man hears its greatness, O king, / attains prosperity, growth, fame, and auspiciousness, and goes to heaven.
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, named 'Description of the Pratipatkalpa', in the Brāhmaparvan of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa, in the collection of fifty thousand verses.
